Kawashima has appeared in numerous television dramas and movies since 2006. In 2017, she received her first leading role as a voice actress in the anime series, Nana Maru San Batsu. She has also voiced characters in the movie "Hunter × Hunter: Phantom Rouge" and the television series "Kōkōsei Restaurant".

In addition to her acting career, Kawashima has been involved in music. She has released acoustic demos and has been featured in Calpis Water commercials. The song "Tsutaetai Koto/I Wanna See You" was used in these commercials. All songs written by Mao Abe.

Between 1981 and 1985, they collaborated on four murals, including "We Are Family" and "Life". Torres' sculptures show an instinctive drive to create tableaux from single figures and are included in the field of humanistic naturalism because they accurately portray people. He met frequent collaborator Ahearn in 1980. After working in New York City, Torres moved to Florida where he currently lives and works. His sculptures are often displayed in public attached to buildings, free standing, and in street events as an element of performance art. Examples of his work include "On Dawson Street", "Double Dutch", and "Back to School". Torres is also considered a community-based artist.

She is the daughter of Francisco Miranda Araya, a municipal worker, and Orfilia de las Mercedes Meneses Roa, a seamstress. Her father passed away when she was six years old. In 2013, Miranda ran for President of Chile, representing the Partido Igualdad (Equality Party). She presented her candidacy on November 5, 2013, with a 125-page document centered on four areas related to social reforms. The four main areas of her program were titled: "Superación del capitalismo" (Overcoming capitalism), "Que el pueblo mande" (Let the people rule), "Recuperación de nuestros derechos" (recovering our rights), and "El buen vivir" (Good living). However, she lost the election.

Later, she became the president of the Partido Igualdad. She was proclaimed presidential candidate representing the party for the 2013 president election on January 20 of that year. Miranda and Marcel Claude's candidacies were negotiating to "unify themselves" into only one candidacy in May 2013, but Miranda ruled out she was resigning her candidacy before the election.

question: Question: Tell me a bio of Bhāskara I.
answer:
Bhāskara I, also known as Bhaskara to avoid confusion with the 12th-century mathematician Bhāskara II, was a 7th-century mathematician from India. He is notable for being the first to write numbers in the Hindu decimal system with a circle for the zero. This innovation greatly simplified the process of mathematical calculations.

In his work, Bhāskara I gave a unique and remarkable rational approximation of the sine function in his commentary on Aryabhata's work, titled "Āryabhaṭīyabhāṣya", which was written in 629 CE. This commentary is among the oldest known prose works in Sanskrit on mathematics and astronomy.

Bhāskara I also wrote two astronomical works in the line of Aryabhata's school, the "Mahābhāskarīya" and the "Laghubhāskarīya". His work on catarchic astrology, titled "Lalla", is one of the earliest known Sanskrit astrological works for determining auspicious and inauspicious times. However, no edition of this text has ever been published, and the known manuscripts are incomplete.

Despite this, Bhāskara I's influence can be seen in the works of later astronomers such as Śrīpati, Vaṭeśvara, and Bhāskara II, who later wrote a commentary on the "Śiṣyadhīvṛddhidatantra". He followed the Ārya-pakṣa or the school of Āryabhaṭa (continued by Bhāskara I), but divided the "mahāyuga" the traditional way, following the Brāhma-pakṣa school of Brahmagupta.

question: Question: Tell me a bio of Robin del Castillo.

Robin del Castillo was born in Cali, Colombia, where he grew up surrounded by music in its purest and most diverse forms. Robin del Castillo specialized in Latin Tropical Music, including Salsa, Merengue, Cumbia, Bachata, Reggaeton, and Latin pop.

In August 2009, he established his own entertainment company, Del Castillo Latin Productions ltd. In September 2009, he hosted the first exclusive live Salsa Concerts in London with Jose Bello, a famous Dominican Salsa singer, and Camilo Azuquita, a Panamanian Salsa singer. This was the first time these two maestros de la salsa performed in London.

Over the past 7 years, Robin Del Castillo has been playing and taking part in the most successful Latin events in London. He has also provided musical accompaniment for several well-known Latin singers, including David Pabon, Pedro Conga, Paquito Guzman, Luisito Carrion, Jose Bello, Mariano Civico, and Roberto Blades, among others. They also regularly perform in private parties.

Robin Del Castillo is currently launching his new album called "Pa’ Mi Tierra" with 10 songs. He is the author and composer of 8 of those songs, and the other 2 are famous romantic Latin songs that he adapted to Salsa music. The album is a mix of several Latin rhythms, including Salsa, Chacha, and Salsaton (a mix of Salsa and Reggaeton). One of the songs, "She's the One," is a Salsaton in Spanglish.

question: Question: Tell me a bio of Jashubhai Dhanabhai Barad.
answer:
Jashubhai Dhanabhai Barad was an Indian politician who served as a member of the 14th Lok Sabha of India, representing the Junagadh constituency of Gujarat. He was born on September 15, 1955, and hailed from the Ahir community. His family was native to Badalpara village near Veraval.

Barad was a former Cabinet Minister of water resources and irrigation of Gujarat state and played a significant role in the development of Narmada and Ukai Dam Projects. He served his fourth term as a member of the legislative assembly representing Talala Gir Constituency of Gujarat until 2016.

He was known as the "lion of saurastra and lion of sorath" and was elected to Lok Sabha in the Indian general election, 2004. He was twice elected to the Gujarat legislative assembly in 1990, 1995, 1998, and 2012 from Somnath and Talala Gir constituencies.

Barad died on January 25, 2016, at Ahmedabad following a brain tumor. After his death, his brother Bhagvanjibhai Barad was elected to the Lok Sabha with a margin of 31,000 votes against the BJP candidate Govindbhai Parmar.

Diego Suarez was a renowned garden designer, born in 1888 in Bogotá, Colombia. He was the son of Roberto Suarez, a Colombian diplomat and historian, and his Italian wife, Maria Costa. After the death of their father, Diego and his siblings spent their childhood in their mother's native country.

Suarez took courses as an architectural designer at the Accademia delle Belle Arti in Florence. There, he was taken under the wing of Arthur Acton, who was restoring the gardens of the Acton villa, Villa La Pietra. Acton introduced Suarez to the formal Renaissance gardening techniques, which he later applied in his work.

One of Suarez's most famous works is the garden design at James Deering's Villa Vizcaya in Miami, Florida. He also served as a press attaché and minister counselor for Chile in Washington, D.C. from 1948 until 1952 and counselor to the Colombian delegation to the United Nations.

In 1937, Suarez married Evelyn Marshall Field, the first wife of department-store heir Marshall Field III and a sister-in-law of the future Brooke Astor. By that marriage, Suarez had three stepchildren: Barbara, Bettine, and Marshall Field IV.

Suarez's work at Villa Vizcaya is characterized by his Baroque taste, contrasts of sun and shade, and many slight changes of level to enliven the essentially flat site. He is interred at Woodlawn Cemetery in The Bronx, New York City.

Francis Nicholson (painter) was a British artist born on November 14, 1753, in Pickering, North Yorkshire. He is primarily recognized as a landscape artist, working in both watercolor and oil. After studying with a local artist in Scarborough, Nicholson began his career in Pickering, creating sporting pictures and portraits for various Yorkshire patrons. By the mid-1780s, he started painting country houses, which led him to focus on landscapes in watercolor.

From 1789, Nicholson contributed views of both Yorkshire and Scotland to exhibitions at the Royal Academy. He also supplied topographical views for the Copper Plate Magazine and collaborated with the engraver Francis Jukes on "Views of England" for the book "The Beauties of England and Wales."

Although his market became increasingly London-based, Nicholson continued to live in Yorkshire, residing in Whitby, Knaresborough, and Ripon before moving to London around 1803. In 1804, he became a founder-member of the Society of Painters in Watercolours and was a regular and prolific contributor to its exhibitions.

Nicholson was known for his temper, as historian George Waller described him as "subject to fits of passion." He was notorious for his outbursts, and an Indian once said of him, "The general is drunk." When informed that Nicholson did not drink alcohol, the Indian replied, "I do not mean that he is drunk with rum, he was born drunk."

question: Question: Tell me a bio of Chris Woakes.
answer:

Woakes began his career with Warwickshire and topped their county bowling averages in 2008. He was selected for the England Lions squad and the preliminary 2009 ICC World Twenty20 championship. He made his Test debut against Australia in the fifth Ashes Test in 2013.

Woakes has had a successful career with the English national team, playing in various formats of the game. In One Day Internationals (ODIs), he has taken numerous wickets and scored runs with the bat. In Tests, he has also taken wickets and contributed with the bat.

In the 2019 ODI series against the West Indies, Woakes took figures of 4–47 as England won by 45 runs. He also made an unbeaten 68 with the bat as England won by four wickets in the second ODI. In the final match of the series, Woakes made 13 and then took figures of 3–16 as England won by 186 runs.

In the 2014 ODI series against Sri Lanka, Woakes took figures of 6–47 in the fifth match of the series as England won the game and the series. He was also trusted with the new ball in the series as senior bowlers Stuart Broad and James Anderson were injured.

Woakes has also played in the Indian Premier League (IPL), making his debut in 2017 for the Kolkata Knight Riders. He was bought for £504,140 (Rs. 4.2 crores) in the players auction for IPL 2017.

Overall, Chris Woakes is a talented and versatile cricketer who has made significant contributions to the English national team in various formats of the game.

question: Question: Tell me a bio of Fidel Castro.
answer:
Fidel Castro was a Cuban revolutionary and politician, born in Birán, Oriente Province in 1926. He was the illegitimate son of Ángel Castro y Argiz, a wealthy farmer and landowner, and his mistress Lina Ruz González.

In his early years, Fidel Castro was educated by a tutor in Santiago de Cuba, and later attended two boarding schools before being sent to El Colegio de Belén, a school run by Jesuits in Havana. In 1945, he began studying law at the University of Havana, where he first became politically active.

Fidel Castro's life and career are detailed in the biography "The Real Fidel Castro," written by British diplomat Sir Leycester Coltman. Coltman served as British ambassador to Cuba from 1991 through to 1994, during which time he got to know Castro personally. The biography looks at Castro's life from its beginning up until the start of the 21st century.

One notable event in Fidel Castro's career was his state visit to Chile in 1971, which was a landmark event for both Chilean internal politics and the foreign relations of Cuba. The visit occurred during the presidency of Salvador Allende and served to break the diplomatic isolation that Cuba had been subject to in Latin America.

Fidel Castro's religious views are also a matter of public interest. According to the "Washington Post," his letters from prison suggest that he was a man of unusual spiritual depth and a fervent believer in God. This is further evidenced by a letter he wrote to the father of a fallen comrade, in which he wrote: "I will not speak of him as if he were absent, he has not been and he will never be."

In later years, Fidel Castro's interactions with the Pope and statements encouraging a more open Cuban society were also significant. On September 20, 2015, he met with Pope Francis during the Pope's three day visit to Cuba, where they discussed protecting the environment and the problems of the modern world.

In 2016, the film "A United Kingdom" told the story of the controversies that surrounded Ian Khama's grandfather's marriage. It starred David Oyelowo as Khama's grandfather and Rosamund Pike as his grandmother. question: Question: Tell me a bio of Jackie Shroff.
answer:
Jackie Shroff, born Jai Krishan Kakubhai Shroff on February 1, 1957, is an Indian actor who has been a significant figure in the Hindi cinema (Bollywood) industry for nearly four decades. He has appeared in over 220 films across eleven languages, including Hindi, Konkani, Kannada, Marathi, Oriya, Punjabi, Bengali, Malayalam, Tamil, Telugu, Bhojpuri, and Gujarati.

Shroff was born in Udgir, Bombay State, India, to Kakulal Harilal Shroff, a Gujarati Hindu, and Amrita Kakulal ("Rita") Shroff, an Uyghur from Kazakhstan. He has no siblings. As a youngster, he modeled in a few advertisements, including Savage perfumes. His classmate in school gave him the name "Jackie," which filmmaker Subhash Ghai later used when he launched Shroff in the film "Hero."

Shroff dropped out of school after his 11th standard. He saw his elder brother drown and die when he himself was just ten, an incident that had a lasting impact on him. His mother protected and cared for him throughout his life.

In 2017, Shroff made his debut in short films with the drama film "Khujli," directed by Sonam Nair. He has also participated in various award shows, such as the Hiru Golden Film Awards 2016 in Sri Lanka, where he was a special guest alongside other Bollywood celebrities like Sunil Shetty, Neil Nitin Mukesh, Sridevi, Madhuri Dixit, and Karishma Kapoor.

Shroff has won three Filmfare Awards among other accolades for his acting performances. Notable films in his career include "Parinda," where he played the role of Kishan, initially offered to Naseeruddin Shah and Nana Patekar. He was hesitant to take the role due to concerns about being typecast, but eventually agreed after listening to the songs from the film.

question: Question: Tell me a bio of Radja Nainggolan.
answer:
Radja Nainggolan is a Belgian professional footballer who plays as a midfielder for Italian club Inter Milan. Born on May 4, 1988, in Antwerp, he is of Flemish ethnicity, but also has Batak roots from his father's side. His mother, Lizy Bogaerts, raised him with his three half brothers and his twin sister.

Nainggolan spent most of his professional career in Italy, representing Piacenza, Cagliari, Roma, and Inter Milan, and making over 290 Serie A appearances. He is nicknamed "Il Ninja."

Nainggolan is a Belgium international, having played for the national team for eight years. He has represented Belgium at Euro 2016 and scored six goals in 30 appearances for his country.

Nainggolan began playing football with Tubantia Borgerhout at the age of 5. Seven years later, he moved to the youth team of Germinal Beerschot, where he remained until 2005, when he was noticed by scouts.

Nainggolan scored his first goal for the "Red Devils" on 5 March 2014, in a friendly draw with Côte d'Ivoire. He was an undisputed starter for the Marc Wilmots-led Red Devils during the UEFA Euro 2016 qualifying campaign, scoring in an away draw with Bosnia and Herzegovina and a 4–1 win in Andorra as the team qualified for the tournament for the first time in 16 years.

In the summer of 2018, Nainggolan signed with Inter Milan for €38 million. He scored in his league debut on 1 September, helping the visitors defeat Bologna 3–0. He also scored the equaliser in a 2–1 comeback win at PSV Eindhoven in the Champions League group stage to become the first-ever Belgian to achieve the feat in the competition for Inter.

Nainggolan's father abandoned the family when he was just a child, and his mother died in 2010. After her death, he tattooed two large wings on his back with her dates of birth and death. He is fluent in Dutch,

question: Question: Tell me a bio of Zeca Pagodinho.
answer:
Zeca Pagodinho is a Brazilian singer-songwriter who works primarily in the genres of samba and pagode. Born on February 4, 1959, in the neighborhood of Irajá, Rio de Janeiro, Zeca grew up surrounded by traditional samba and started making his own verses while still a child at GRES Portela samba school. In the 1970s, he began frequenting the Carnival Block of Cacique de Ramos, which became a significant hub for pagode.

In the early 1980s, after a period of eclipse due to the popularity of disco and Brazilian rock, samba reemerged in the media with a musical movement originating from the suburbs. During this time, Zeca's skills caught the attention of samba singer Beth Carvalho, who invited him to record the song "Camarão Que Dorme a Onda Leva" in 1983. This marked the beginning of Zeca's recording career, and he has since released 15 albums and three DVDs.

Zeca's creative, joyful, and sometimes mischievous songs reflect the everyday life of the typical easy-going carioca (resident of Rio de Janeiro) and have been very successful in Brazil. He is one of the country's biggest-selling artists. Zeca lives in the neighborhood of Barra da Tijuca with his wife Mônica Silva and their children Eduardo, Elisa, Louis, and Maria Eduarda. In 2015, his album "Ser Humano" was nominated for the 16th Latin Grammy Awards in the Best Samba/Pagode Album category.

question: Question: Tell me a bio of Riccardo Tisci.
answer:
Riccardo Tisci is an Italian fashion designer, born in 1974. He studied at the Design Istituto d’Arte Applicata in Cantù, Italy, until the age of 17, and then graduated from London's Central Saint Martins Academy in 1999.

Before joining Givenchy, Tisci worked for companies such as Puma and Coccapani, and spent time living in India, where he began to work on his own collection. He also had a three-year contract with Ruffo Research, a company that has helped launch the careers of several fashion designers.

In 2005, Tisci was named artistic director of womenswear for Givenchy, where he has had particular success in haute couture. He has expanded the chromatic palette of the house, incorporating flashy colors such as baby blue and red blood, and incorporating metal, wildlife, and floral prints into his designs. Tisci's runway presentations are highly stylized in terms of architecture and space.

Tisci has collaborated with several high-profile artists, including Jay-Z, Kanye West, and Alexander McQueen. He has also worked on the covers for "Watch the Throne", "H•A•M", and "Otis" with Jay-Z and Kanye West, and on the album "Cruel Summer" with Kanye West's label GOOD Music.

In February 2017, Tisci stepped down as creative director of Givenchy, stating that he now wishes to focus on his personal interests and passions. It is not known if he has any plans to work with an Iranian brand, as he has mentioned in an interview that he would like to do so.

Vijay has a significant following not only in India but also in Japan, the UK, France, and China. His films are released in five continents and more than eighty countries.

Vijay made his cinematic debut at the age of ten in the drama "Vetri" (1984). He gained recognition for his roles in films like "Love Today" (1997), "Once More", "Nerukku Ner", "Kadhalukku Mariyadhai", and "Thulladha Manamum Thullum" (1999), for which he won a Tamil Nadu State Film Award for Best Actor.

Throughout his career, Vijay has been involved in various social welfare activities. Many second-generation Sinaloan traffickers, including Rafael Caro Quintero, Ernesto Fonseca Carrillo, and Joaquín 'El Chapo' Guzmán, claim to have learned their trade while serving in the Avilés organization, which was a part of the Guadalajara Cartel.

question: Question: Tell me a bio of Karl Eliasberg.
answer:
Karl Eliasberg (June 10, 1907 – February 12, 1978) was a Soviet conductor, born in Minsk. He graduated from the Leningrad Conservatory as a violinist in 1929 and was conductor of the Leningrad Theatre of Musical Comedy from 1929 to 1931 before joining Leningrad Radio as conductor.

During the siege of Leningrad, Eliasberg played a significant role in society and culture when Dmitri Shostakovich dedicated his Seventh Symphony to the city. The symphony, also known as the "Leningrad Symphony," was performed by the Leningrad Radio Orchestra, which Eliasberg conducted, and was heard over the radio, lifting the spirits of the survivors.

Eliasberg was recognized as a Meritorious Artist of the RSFSR in 1944. However, after the war, Yevgeny Mravinsky returned and blocked Eliasberg's career in Leningrad, causing him to become a traveling provincial conductor. Between 1945 and 1975, Eliasberg headlined in Leningrad only three more times, each time conducting the Seventh Symphony with the reserve orchestra.

In 1961, he conducted the 1st movement only, and in 1964, there was a reunion of Eliasberg and 22 of the original musicians before a performance in Shostakovich's presence. This was the first time they had been together in 22 years. The survivors played in their same seats, and the audience gave a standing ovation.

Eliasberg later wrote that the third time he conducted the Seventh Symphony was on May 9, 1975, three years before his death. After his death in 1978, his ashes were buried in a small plot at the back of the Piskaryovskoye Memorial Cemetery.

Mackwell is an internationally recognized researcher in the field of geophysics, specializing in laboratory-based studies of the physical, chemical, and mechanical properties of geological materials. question: Question: Tell me a bio of D. B. Nihalsinghe.
answer:
D. B. Nihalsinghe, born on May 27, 1939, and passed away on April 21, 2016, was a highly accomplished Sri Lankan film director, cinematographer, editor, producer, and administrator. He was known for his versatility in various fields, including film, television, and education.

Nihalsinghe was a pioneer in introducing professional television production to Sri Lanka, starting with the country's and South Asia's first color teledrama, "Dimuthu Muthu," in 1979. He served as the founding Chief Executive Officer and General Manager of Sri Lanka's National Film Corporation.

Before his career in film and television, Nihalsinghe was an accomplished student leader, serving as Head Prefect and Sergeant of the cadet platoon at Ananda College. He initially aspired to join the army but developed an interest in film after receiving a 16mm Bolex cine camera as a gift for completing his SSC examination from his father, veteran journalist D.B Dhanapala.

Nihalsinghe entered the University of Ceylon and later made significant contributions to the Sri Lankan film industry. Some of his notable films include "Ridei Nimanaya" and "Kelimadala," the latter of which won the highest number of national awards at the time.

In addition to his film and television work, Nihalsinghe also authored a book titled "Failure in Sri Lanka," published by Trafford Publishing, British Columbia, Canada. He was also a teacher and shared his knowledge and expertise in the field of film and television.

question: Question: Tell me a bio of Joseph Jaquet.
answer:
Joseph Jaquet was a Belgian sculptor born on January 30, 1822, in Antwerp, Belgium. He was the son of a baker and studied at the Brussels Académie Royale des Beaux-Arts under Guillaume Geefs. He was also friends with Peter Ludwig Kühnen, a painter from Aachen who specialized in romantic landscapes.

Jaquet's brother Jacques also assisted him throughout his lifetime and contributed to sculpture with his own productions for the Brussels art salons.

Jaquet's career took off in 1842 when he exhibited a marble bust, three plaster busts, a "Moses Saved from the Waters" and a "Meditating Saint Paul" at the Brussels Art Salon, which brought him notoriety. He gained more recognition in 1854 with "The Golden Age."

Throughout his career, Jaquet received several commissions, including a statue of Louise of Orléans, first Queen of the Belgians, which was on the "Place d'Armes" in Philippeville and was later moved to the old "École moyenne," Namur street. He also designed a statue for the Brussels Stock Exchange and an equestrian statue of Baldwin I of Constantinople for the national monument in The Hague.

Jaquet was a professor at the Brussels Académie Royale des Beaux-Arts and a master of Charles Samuel. He died in 1898 in Schaerbeek in the Brussels-Capital Region.

Josh Mansour (Arabic: جوش منصور; born 17 June 1990) is a rugby league footballer who plays for the Penrith Panthers in the National Rugby League. He was born in Sydney, New South Wales, Australia. Mansour is of Lebanese descent through his father Fidel, who was born north of Beirut, Portuguese descent through his mother Angie, who was born in Madeira, and Cuban descent.

Mansour primarily plays on the wing, although he has also played as a fullback. He has represented Australia and Lebanon internationally, as well as the New South Wales State of Origin, Prime Minister's XIII, and NSW City Origin teams.

Mansour started his junior rugby league career with the Penrith Panthers. He made his NRL debut in 2012 and scored two tries in his debut year. In 2013, he played in 14 matches and scored 4 tries.

In 2014, Mansour extended his contract with the Panthers to the end of the 2014 season. He had a breakout season in 2015, finishing the year as the Panthers' highest try-scorer with 16 tries. He was awarded as the Winger of the Year at the 2016 Dally M Awards night.

In 2016, Mansour featured in all 3 matches for the New South Wales Blues on the wing in their 2-1 series loss in the State of Origin series. He also played in one match of the Australian 2016 Four Nations tournament.

In 2017, Mansour suffered a serious knee injury during a training session, ruling him out for the rest of the season. He returned to the field in 2018 and signed a three-year contract extension to stay at Penrith until the end of the 2021 season.

Mansour is an avid fan of Arsenal F.C. and his wife Daniella gave birth to their first child, Siana, on 2 November 2017.

question: Question: Tell me a bio of Abraham Ancer.
answer:
Abraham Ancer is a Mexican professional golfer who was born on February 27, 1991, in McAllen, Texas, but was raised in Reynosa, Mexico. He holds dual American and Mexican citizenship. Ancer played college golf at Odessa College and the University of Oklahoma, graduating in 2013. During his one year at Odessa, he was a first-team All-American and finished in a tie for second in the Junior College National Golf Championship. At Oklahoma, he saw his most success during his first year, winning twice.

After turning professional in 2013, Ancer played on the Web.com Tour in 2015, where he finished runner-up at the Brasil Champions in March and won the Nova Scotia Open in July. He finished 11th in the regular season money list, which earned him a PGA Tour card for the 2016 season. However, he couldn't maintain his card for the entire year.

In the 2017 season, Ancer had five top-5 finishes, including three runner-up finishes, on the Web.com Tour, which secured him a PGA Tour card for the 2018 season by finishing in third place on the regular season money list. In the 2018 season, he had a good start with top-5 finishes in the CIMB Classic and the Shriners Hospitals for Children Open, results that lifted him into the world top-100 for the first time. He followed this up with a 5-stroke victory in the Australian Open, a week before representing Mexico in the World Cup of Golf.

In the PGA Tour season 2018, Ancer earned US$1.7 million and finished 60th in the FedEx Cup. He also had an entry to the 2018 Open Championship, his first major championship, but missed the cut. In the 2018–19 season, he had a good performance at the Open Championship, where he had rounds of 71 and 78.

Ancer had a significant achievement in his college career, as he had the sixth-lowest scoring average in Oklahoma history of 72.03. During his entire career, he ended up second in all-time scoring average.

question: Question: Tell me a bio of Shoya Nakajima.
answer:
Shoya Nakajima is a Japanese professional footballer who has represented various national teams at different age levels. He first gained recognition when he was selected for the Japanese under-17 national team in May 2011, for the Slovakia Cup, a tournament that served as preparation for the FIFA U-17 World Cup. In the U-17 World Cup held in Mexico, Nakajima appeared in two matches and scored one goal in a 3-2 loss against Brazil in the quarter-finals.

In August 2013, he was called for the Japanese under-20 national team to participate in the L'Alcúdia International Football Tournament. He made his debut for the Japanese national team on 23 March 2013, scoring his first goal against Mali in a 1-1 draw.

Nakajima's career highlights include winning the U-17 World Cup in 2011, where he scored a double in the extra-time of the quarter-finals match against Iraq and was crowned the Most Valuable Player of the Tournament. He was also a part of the Japanese Olympic national team (under-23) that competed in the 2016 Summer Olympics in Rio de Janeiro, where he scored a goal against Colombia.

In international competitions, Nakajima has also played for the Japanese under-23 national team in the 2013 AFC U-22 Championship, the 2014 Asian Games, and the 2016 AFC U-23 Championship. He has scored goals against various teams including Iraq, Iran, Australia, Nepal, Palestine, and Argentina.

As of now, Nakajima plays for the Japanese J1 League club, Cerezo Osaka. He has been a consistent performer for the club and has contributed significantly to their success.

question: Question: Tell me a bio of Celâl Bayar.
answer:
Celâl Bayar was a significant Turkish politician who served as the third President of Turkey from 1950 to 1960 and previously as Prime Minister from 1937 to 1939. He was born on May 16, 1883, and passed away on August 22, 1986.

In the early stages of his career, Bayar served as the Minister of the Economy in 1921 and led the negotiation commission during Çerkes Ethem's uprising. He was a member of the Turkish delegation during the Lausanne Peace Conference in 1922, serving as an advisor to İsmet İnönü. After the elections in 1923, he served as the deputy of İzmir in the Parliament.

Bayar was appointed Minister of Exchange Construction and Settlement in 1924, during which time he founded Türkiye İş Bankası in Ankara. The bank was established with donations of gold bullion sent by the government following the closing stages of World War I on the side of the Allies. Atatürk appointed Bayar, his close aide, as the president of the newly formed bank.

In the latter part of his career, Bayar played a significant role in the political landscape of Turkey. In 1949, Turkey became a member of the Council of Europe. The Democratic Party established by Bayar won the 1950, 1954, and 1957 general elections and stayed in power for a decade, with Adnan Menderes as the Prime Minister and Bayar as the President.

As the Turkish President, Bayar was decorated with the Legion of Merit by the President of the United States, as a result of Turkey's participation in the Korean War. He is considered to be the longest-lived former head of state until 8 December 2008, when he was surpassed by Chau Sen Cocsal Chhum.

question: Question: Tell me a bio of Annie Landouw.
answer:
Annie Landouw (also Landauw, 1913 – 17 August 1982) was an Indonesian "keroncong" singer and film actress. She was born in Surakarta, Central Java, in 1913. Landouw lost her sight following an extended illness as a child, and was not long afterwards adopted by her aunt and uncle. In 1927 she competed in and won her first singing competition, a Concours concert at a night fair in Surakarta. As a result, she was approached by Beka, a recording company, which signed her. She moved to Batavia (now Jakarta), the capital of the Dutch East Indies, soon after.

Landouw quickly rose in popularity and by 1938 she had joined the NIROM radio troupe, singing "keroncong". The following year she joined Hugo Dumas' troupe Lief Java. During this period she became active in film. In 1938 she provided vocals for "Fatima", a production by Tan's Film; she provided vocals again for Tan's 1939 film "Gagak Item" ("Black Raven"). She made her onscreen debut later that year, with "Siti Akbari". In 1940 she appeared in two further films, "Sorga Ka Toedjoe" ("Seventh Heaven") and "Roekihati".

Landouw's prowess singing "keroncong" rendered her immensely popular. In 1940, the blind singer was scheduled to appear in a film titled "Roekiah", in which she played the role of a blind woman reunited with her estranged husband. This film was a commercial success, and the reviews were positive.

After Indonesia's independence, Landouw continued singing; however, she acted in no further films. She died on 17 August 1982. Music scholar Peter Keppy suggests that, because of her popularity as a "keroncong" singer, Landouw may have influenced the character of Yah in Armijn Pane's 1940 novel "Belenggu"; in the novel, Yah is famous as a "keroncong" singer under the stage name Siti Hayati.

Vishal has an elder brother, Vikram Krishna, who has produced several of his films and a younger sister, Aishwarya.

He produces films under his production company, Vishal Film Factory.

In addition to his acting career, Vishal has also been involved in Tamil film association elections. He has contested and won two important elections against stiff opposition. His last release "Thupparivaalan" was a hit, and his next film "Irumbu Thirai" is due in January.

question: Question: Tell me a bio of Kevin De Bruyne.
answer:
Kevin De Bruyne is a Belgian professional footballer who currently plays as a midfielder for English club Manchester City and the Belgian national team. He was born on June 28, 1991. De Bruyne started his career at Genk, where he was a regular player when they won the 2010–11 Belgian Pro League. In 2012, he joined English club Chelsea, but later moved to Wolfsburg in 2014 before joining Manchester City.

De Bruyne's playing style has frequently been ranked among the best in Europe, and he has often been described as a "complete" footballer. He was ranked the fourth-best footballer in the world by "The Guardian" in 2017.

De Bruyne has been involved in several notable events off the field as well. In 2014, he was an ambassador for the Special Olympics and was involved in a controversial advertisement campaign on his personal Instagram account. The campaign used the slogan "Would you still be my fan if I looked like this?" and depicted De Bruyne resembling a person with Down syndrome, which sparked controversy.

In 2015, De Bruyne bought his first car, a Mercedes, in preparation for the birth of his son, Mason Milian De Bruyne, who was born on March 10, 2016. De Bruyne and his partner, Michèle Lacroix, married in June 2017.

On the field, De Bruyne has scored several notable goals for Manchester City, including a stunning goal against Paris Saint-Germain in the Champions League and a goal from a free kick against FC Barcelona. He has also been awarded the "Man of the Match" on several occasions, including in a 4–0 win over Bournemouth in 2016.

Overall, Kevin De Bruyne is a highly skilled and accomplished footballer who has made a significant impact on the field for both Manchester City and the Belgian national team.

question: Question: Tell me a bio of Joji (musician).
answer:
Joji (musician), whose real name is George Miller, was born on September 18, 1992. He is a Japanese singer, songwriter, rapper, record producer, and former YouTube personality and comedian. Miller grew up in Osaka, Japan, and his music is inspired by his time there as well as boom bap instrumentals he listened to while attending Canadian Academy.

Miller's start as an entertainer began on his now defunct YouTube channels, DizastaMusic and TVFilthyFrank, where he created rap songs, rants, extreme challenges, ukulele performances, and a bizarre show, with most of the main characters played by Miller including the titular character of Filthy Frank. Miller also produced comedy hip hop music under the name Pink Guy.

After relocating to Manhattan, New York, Miller expanded upon his music career by starting his Pink Guy persona, which paved the way for his Joji persona. Miller originally announced his Joji album on May 3, 2014, alongside the first Pink Guy album. However, Miller subtly transitioned from his YouTube career to his music career as Joji, stating to "Billboard" "now I get to do stuff that I want to hear."

Joji for the first time performed on May 18, 2017, in Los Angeles. His debut single from his debut commercial project, "In Tongues," was released on October 17, 2017, and the EP of the same name was released on November 3, 2017, by Empire Distribution. A deluxe version of the EP was released on February 14, 2018, with 8 remixes of songs from the EP along with the release of "Plastic Taste" and "I Don't Wanna."

Miller currently lives in Brooklyn, New York, and often flies to Los Angeles for work, where he has a residence. Miller has an undisclosed neurological condition that causes stress-induced seizures, which is one of the reasons that led him to quit his YouTube career.

question: Question: Tell me a bio of Ameyaw Debrah.
answer:
Ameyaw Debrah, known professionally as Ameyaw Debrah, is a Ghanaian celebrity blogger, freelance journalist, and reporter. He founded AmeyawDebrah.com, an entertainment website and blog that primarily publishes news about Ghanaian celebrities. Debrah graduated from Kwame Nkrumah University of Science and Technology with a bachelor's degree in Publishing. While at KNUST, he won the Best Publishing Student award in 2005.

He has made significant contributions to several pan-African websites, including Jamati.com, Orijin-ent.com, and ModernGhana.com. In 2008, he joined GhanaWeb.com as the entertainment editor, and launched his own website in the same year. Through his work, Debrah has had the opportunity to interview numerous personalities, including Kofi Annan, Rev. Jesse Jackson, Lloyd, John Legend, Damon Dash, Ade Bantu, Trey Songz, Amber Rose, Ludacris, Coptic, Wyclef Jean, Mario, Eve, Sean Paul, Jimmy Jean-Louis, David Clowney, Santonio Holmes, Majid Michel, Nadia Buari, and John Dumelo.

In addition to his work in journalism, Debrah is also involved in managing the interests of Coptic, a Multi-Platinum award-winning Ghanaian music producer, in Ghana and Africa. He is also in charge of scouting for new up and coming talents that can be signed to Rebel Musik, Coptic’s African music production branch. Debrah also managed multiple-award-winning rapper Pappy Kojo in 2014.

In 2015, Debrah launched the My Ghana Campaign, a platform where readers can record a one-minute video discussing relevant issues in Ghana. From September 2015, he worked as the editor-in-chief of a newly established publication called yen.com.gh. He left the role in September 2017. Debrah contributes to StarGist (an entertainment segment on Africa Magic) as a Skype correspondent. He also contributes to content on EbonyLife TV and "Glitz Africa Magazine". He is an ambassador for Malta

question: Question: Tell me a bio of Fahadh Faasil.
answer:
Fahadh Faasil is an Indian film actor and producer who primarily works in the Malayalam film industry. He began his film career at the age of 19 with the romantic film "Kaiyethum Doorath" (2002), directed by his father Fazil, but the film was a critical and commercial failure. After a six-year hiatus, Fahadh made his comeback with the anthology film "Kerala Cafe" (2009), in the short film "Mrityunjayam." He gained public attention for his role as Arjun in the thriller film "Chaappa Kurishu" (2011).

Fahadh won his first Kerala State Film Award for Best Supporting Actor for his role in the film "Diamond Necklace" (2012), where he portrayed Dr. Arun Kumar, a Dubai-based oncologist. He went on to win the Film Award for Best Actor for his performances as Michael in "Artist" and Harikrishnan in "North 24 Kaatham." He also won his second Filmfare Award for Best Actor for his role in "North 24 Kaatham."

Fahadh has appeared in several advertisements, including Titan, Milma, and Adithi aata. He married Malayalam and Tamil film actress Nazriya Nazim on 21 August 2014. The pair had gotten to know each other more on the sets of Anjali Menon's "Bangalore Days" (2014), in which they were playing husband and wife. Fahadh had roles as Mahesh Bhavana in "Maheshinte Prathikaaram" (2016), Indian diplomat Manoj Abraham in "Take Off" (2017), and in other notable films. He also produced and starred as Aloshy in the 2014 period film "Iyobinte Pusthakam" under his production company, Fahadh Faasil and Friends Pvt Ltd.

question: Question: Tell me a bio of Cleopatra.
answer:
Cleopatra, most famously known as Cleopatra VII, was the last active ruler of the Ptolemaic Kingdom of Egypt. She was born around 69 BC and is believed to have been the daughter of Ptolemy XII Auletes and Cleopatra V, although this is not definitively confirmed.

Cleopatra's early life was marked by political maneuverings. Her mother, Cleopatra III, was a queen consort of Egypt, and Cleopatra Selene, Cleopatra VII's sister, was a monarch of Syria. Cleopatra VII's father, Ptolemy XII, expelled Cleopatra III from Egypt, leaving Cleopatra VII behind. It is believed that Cleopatra VII then married her brother Ptolemy XIII, although this is a subject of debate.

Cleopatra VII is perhaps best known for her relationships with Julius Caesar and Mark Antony, two of the most powerful figures of the Roman Republic. After the death of Ptolemy XII, Cleopatra VII returned to Egypt and seized the throne, with the help of Julius Caesar. She later had a son, Caesarion, with Caesar.

After Caesar's assassination, Cleopatra VII allied with Mark Antony. Their relationship led to the Battle of Actium in 31 BC, which resulted in the defeat of Antony and Cleopatra. Antony committed suicide, and Cleopatra was captured by Octavian (later known as Augustus Caesar). She is said to have died in 30 BC, possibly by allowing an asp to bite her.

Cleopatra VII is remembered for her intelligence, beauty, and political acumen. She was fluent in several languages, including Greek, Egyptian, and Latin. Her reign marked the end of the Ptolemaic Kingdom and the beginning of Roman Egypt.

Other Cleopatras mentioned in the passages include Cleopatra V, who was presumably the mother of Cleopatra VII, and Cleopatra VI Tryphaena, who may have been Ptolemy's wife, not his daughter. However, these Cleopatras are less well-known and less documented in history compared to Cleopatra VII.

question: Question: Tell me a bio of Jacques Cousteau.
answer:
Jacques Cousteau was a French naval officer, explorer, conservationist, filmmaker, innovator, scientist, photographer, author, and researcher. He was born on June 11, 1910, and passed away on June 25, 1997. Cousteau is best known for his work studying the sea and all forms of life in water.

He co-developed the Aqua-lung, a device that allows divers to breathe underwater for extended periods, revolutionizing the field of underwater exploration. Cousteau was also a pioneer in marine conservation and a member of the Académie française.

In a Chapter entitled "The Holy Scriptures and The Environment" in the posthumous work "The Human, the Orchid, and the Octopus", he is quoted as stating that "The glory of nature provides evidence that God exists".

Cousteau's work has been documented in films, including "Voyage to the Edge of the World" (1976), which he co-directed with his son Philippe Cousteau and Marshall Flaum. The film follows a four-month expedition through Antarctica undertaken between the end of 1972 and the beginning of 1973.

Cousteau was the father of Jean-Michel Cousteau, who is also an oceanographic explorer, environmentalist, educator, and film producer. Cousteau was married to Simone Melchior, and they had three children together.

question: Question: Tell me a bio of Patricia Cladis.

Patricia Cladis (1937 - July 3, 2017) was a Canadian American physicist who specialized in the physics of liquid crystals. She was born in Shanghai and attended high school at Little Flower Academy in Vancouver, BC, graduating in 1955. In 1959, she earned her B.A. in combined Honours Mathematics and Physics from the University of British Columbia. She then went on to acquire her M.A. in Physics from the University of Toronto in 1960.

After receiving her master's degree, Cladis joined Transport Canada as a meteorologist before moving on to be a Programmer-Analyst at KCS Ltd. in 1962. She was appointed an Assistant Professor of Physics at Western Connecticut State University in 1963. For the following four years until 1968, she worked as a Research Assistant at the University of Rochester while she did her graduate studies, where she received her PhD in Physics with a concentration in superconductivity in 1968.

After her PhD, Cladis worked as a research physicist at Bell Labs beginning in 1972. She was a fellow of the American Physical Society and also received a Guggenheim fellowship. Her more recent interests were patterns in complex fluids, which includes polymers, and she wrote a book in 1995 about patterns in complex systems. One example of the applications of liquid crystals is in LCD displays. She was the author or co-author of more than 130 publications and the editor for multiple books. The best-known book that she edited was published in 1995 entitled "Spatio-temporal patterns in nonequilibrium complex systems". Cladis died on July 3, 2017, in Summit, New Jersey.

In 2006, South African President Thabo Mbeki awarded Toms with the Order of the Baobab for his stance against Apartheid and his service. At the time of his death in 2008, Toms was serving as the Director of Health for the city of Cape Town. A eulogy for Toms was held at St. George's Cathedral in Cape Town, with Archbishop Tutu among the attendees.

question: Question: Tell me a bio of Flávio Rocha.
answer:
Flávio Rocha is a Brazilian businessman and former federal deputy, born on February 14, 1958. He is currently the CEO and Chairman of Lojas Riachuelo, one of the largest retailers in Brazil. His family also owns Confecções Guararapes, the group’s industrial company, and Transportadora Casa Verde, the Group's logistics subsidiary. Riachuelo is one of the 15 biggest employers of the country, with over 40,000 employees (2017).

In the political sphere, Rocha served as a federal deputy from 1987 to 1995. He was one of the first businessmen to support the "impeachment" of former president Dilma Rousseff and the candidacy of João Doria to become mayor of São Paulo. In January 2018, Rocha launched the manifesto "Brasil 200", which defends a liberal economic agenda and conservatism in social values.

His grandfather, Waldemar Zveiter, was a close friend and lawyer of Roberto Marinho, founder of Organizações Globo.

question: Question: Tell me a bio of Mindy Smith.
answer:
Mindy Smith is an American singer-songwriter, born on June 1, 1972, on Long Island, New York. She was adopted at birth by a non-denominational Protestant minister and his wife, who was choir director at the church. After her mother died of cancer in 1991, Smith attended Cincinnati Bible College for two years.

Smith moved to Knoxville, Tennessee, where she began listening to folk and bluegrass music, including Alison Krauss and the Cox Family. Her musical career took off when she sang a cover version of Dolly Parton's "Jolene," which led to her first record deal.

In her career, Mindy Smith has released several studio albums, including "One Moment More" (2004), "Long Island Shores" (2006), "My Holiday" (2007), "Stupid Love" (2009), "Mindy Smith" (2012), and "Married but Still Living" (2015). She has also collaborated with artists like Kenny Chesney on the song "Better Boat."

In addition to her music, Smith has been involved in charitable work. In March 2013, she worked with Anthropologie during an in-store performance to raise money and awareness for the Captain Planet Foundation.

Smith has also been open about her personal struggles, including her battle with obsessive–compulsive disorder, which she disclosed in September 2009 while promoting her album "Stupid Love."

question: Question: Tell me a bio of Deitrick Haddon.
answer:
Deitrick Haddon is an American gospel singer, songwriter, music producer, pastor, and actor, born on May 17, 1973. He is best known for his progressive gospel and contemporary styles of music. Haddon launched his solo career as a Christian R&B vocalist with the album "Lost & Found" on Tyscot/Verity in 2002, which peaked at No. 1 on Billboard's Top Gospel Charts and received wide critical acclaim, spawning the hit "Sinner's Prayer."

Haddon has released several albums throughout his career, including "Church on the Moon," which debuted at No. 1 on the Billboard Top Gospel charts and No. 65 on the Billboard 200. He is also part of the cast of the reality television show "Preachers of L.A.," which chronicles the lives of six Los Angeles preachers, including Haddon. The show began airing on October 9, 2013, and airs on the Oxygen network in the United States.

Haddon is married to his second wife, Dominique Haddon (née McTyre), and they are the parents of two daughters, Destin and Denver, and one son, Deitrick.

In addition to his music and acting career, Haddon has also released the album "Revealed," which charted at number 98 on the Billboard 200 and number 2 on the Top Gospel Charts. The album spawned three singles, including "I'm Alive," "Love Him Like I Do" (Featuring Ruben Studdard and Mary Mary), and "I Need Your Help." Music videos were made for all three singles.

In 1856, he married his cousin Frances Hubbard. Grimshaw is best known for his nocturnal scenes of urban landscapes and is considered one of the most renowned painters of the Victorian era, as well as one of the best and most accomplished nightscape and townscape artists of all time.

Grimshaw's early paintings were signed "JAG", "J. A. Grimshaw", or "John Atkinson Grimshaw", though he finally settled on "Atkinson Grimshaw". His accuracy and drive for realism were criticized by some contemporaries, with one critic claiming that his paintings appeared to ‘showed no marks of handling or brushwork’, adding that ‘not a few artists doubted whether they could be accepted as paintings at all’. However, other contemporaries recognized his mastery of lighting and technique, and James McNeill Whistler, whom Grimshaw would go on to work with in his Chelsea studios, stated, “I considered myself the inventor of nocturnes until I saw Grimmy’s moonlit pictures”.

question: Question: Tell me a bio of Imbolo Mbue.
answer:
Imbolo Mbue is a Cameroonian-American author who was born and raised in Limbe, Cameroon. She moved to the United States to attend Rutgers University, where she earned a bachelor's degree in journalism and African studies. After graduation, she worked as a freelance journalist and later as a lawyer.

In 2014, Mbue signed a million-dollar deal with Random House for her debut manuscript, which was later published as Behold the Dreamers in 2016. The novel details the experiences of two New York City families during the 2008 financial crisis, focusing on an immigrant family from Cameroon and their wealthy employers.

Behold the Dreamers received critical acclaim and was a commercial success. It won the PEN/Faulkner Award in 2017 and was selected by Oprah Winfrey for her book club. Mbue's novel was also depicted in the 2015 movie "The Big Short."

In addition to Behold the Dreamers, Mbue has written for various publications, including The New York Times, The Wall Street Journal, and The Washington Post. She currently lives in New York City.

question: Question: Tell me a bio of Shigeru Fukudome.
answer:
Shigeru Fukudome was born in Yonago, Tottori prefecture. He graduated from the 40th class of the Imperial Japanese Naval Academy in 1913, ranking 8 out of 144 cadets. As a midshipman, he served on the cruisers "Soya" and "Izumo" and battleship "Satsuma". After his promotion to ensign, he was assigned to the battleship "Hizen" and cruiser "Kashima". After attending torpedo school and naval artillery school, he served on the patrol boat "Manshu", followed by the cruiser "Chitose" and was promoted to lieutenant in 1918. After attending navigational training, he was assigned as chief navigator to the destroyer "Sakura", and cruiser "Niitaka".

During World War II, Fukudome held several important positions. In late October 1944, due to heavy losses of Japanese air units in the Philippines, his responsibility was expanded to cover the Philippines as well. He moved his headquarters to Manila on October 22. In January 1945, the 2nd Air Fleet was dissolved and merged with the 1st Air Fleet. With the merger of the two air fleets in the Philippines, Fukudome became commander-in-chief of the 6th Air Base and 2nd.

However, after the war, Fukudome was arrested by the British government at the instigation of American prosecutors and accused of war crimes. He was tried by a military tribunal in Singapore. Despite the high regard and trust extended by American and British officers due to Fukudome’s cooperative behavior and attitude, he was arrested once the task of repatriation was accomplished.

Fukudome is also known for being the first flag officer in Japanese history to be captured by the enemy, after his plane crash landed in a storm near Cebu in the Marianas Islands. This event occurred after the death of Admiral Koga, for whom Fukudome had been serving as commander-in-chief of the 6th Air Base and 2nd. The battle plans fell into American hands after his capture.

question: Question: Tell me a bio of 14th Dalai Lama.
answer:
The 14th Dalai Lama, whose religious name is Tenzin Gyatso, was born on July 6, 1935, in Taktser, Amdo, Tibet. He is the current Dalai Lama and is an important monk of the Gelug school, the newest school of Tibetan Buddhism. From the time of the 5th Dalai Lama to 1959, the central government of Tibet, the Ganden Phodrang, invested the position of Dalai Lama with temporal duties.

The Dalai Lama was selected as the tulku (reincarnation) of the 13th Dalai Lama. He was recognized at the age of two and was enthroned at the age of four. He received his monastic education at the Drepung Monastery in Lhasa, Tibet.

The 14th Dalai Lama has been a prominent figure in the Tibetan independence movement and has been a strong advocate for peace, compassion, and the preservation of Tibetan culture and Buddhism. He was forced to flee Tibet in 1959 after a failed uprising against Chinese rule. He has since lived in exile in India, where he established a government-in-exile and a network of Tibetan settlements.

The Dalai Lama has received numerous awards and honors, including the Nobel Peace Prize in 1989. In 2012, he was awarded the Templeton Prize, which he donated to an Indian charity, "Save the Children".

The question of the succession of the 14th Dalai Lama is a controversial issue, as the Chinese government has expressed an interest in choosing the next Dalai Lama. However, according to Buddhist doctrine, the current Dalai Lama is believed to be able to choose the body into which he is reincarnated. The selection process is the responsibility of the High Lamas of the Gelgupa tradition and the Tibetan government. The search can take a long time, as it took four years to find the 14th Dalai Lama. The Dalai Lama has also expressed concern that the Chinese government may manipulate the selection process in order to choose a successor who will go along with their political goals.

question: Question: Tell me a bio of Jesse Chacón.
answer:
Jesse Chacón was a Venezuelan military officer, engineer, and politician born on November 9, 1965. He graduated from the Military Academy in 1987, obtaining a degree in Military Arts and was among the best of his class, "Tomás Montilla Padrón." In 1996, he received his degree in systems engineering from the Polytechnic University of the National Armed Forces (UNEFA) with the honors of Summa Cum Laude. He also completed postgraduate studies in Telematics at the National Institute of Telecommunications in France and the Simón Bolívar University in Caracas.

Jesse Chacón served as the first Minister of Communications in July 2003, where he proposed expanding the coverage of the frequency modulation (FM) in the whole country with more than 35 radio stations. He also started the process of technological upgrading and initiated the creation of the Bolivarian National Police and Experimental Security University.

Chacón chaired the National Commission on the Penitentiary Emergency and the National Committee of Risk Management. He was the head of the Anti-Corruption Presidential Commission and Presidential Commission for Police Reform, as well as the new Administrative System of Identification, Migration, and Immigration of Venezuela. He also guided the automatization of the Civil Registries and Notaries System and of the Police Coordination System and Emergency Response number 171.

On January 9, 2007, Chacón was appointed as Minister of Telecommunications and Informatics, where he focused on issues related to identities, strategic communication, and social networks. In February 2013, he was appointed as a member of the Board of the National System of Youth and Children Orchestras and Choirs of Venezuela, where he was entrusted to make visible the social contribution of the foundation and its significance as a means to include thousands of children and young people in the country. In April 2013, he was designated Minister of Electric Power, where he introduced the program “Gran Misión Electrica Venezuela.”

question: Question: Tell me a bio of Ted Mack (politician).

Mack served for only two terms in both the New South Wales state seat of North Shore and the federal seat of North Sydney to avoid receiving a parliamentary pension. He was elected as an independent Republican delegate to the Australian Constitutional Convention and opposed the model favored by the Australian Republican Movement. Along with Clem Jones, he was a director of Real Republic and was appointed to the official ten-person "no" committee for the 1999 referendum.

In 1997, Mack was elected as one of the one hundred "National Living Treasures," organized by the National Trust of Australia. In 2016, it was reported that Mack had commenced treatment for brain cancers following the discovery of multiple small tumors in his brain. Mack informed the media that the diagnosis was terminal. The inaugural Ted Mack Oration was hosted by North Sydney Council and delivered in his honor.

Mack died after a stroke on November 6, 2018. He was a prominent figure in Australian politics and will be remembered for his independent spirit and contributions to the political landscape.

Tom Coburn is an American politician and physician who was born on March 14, 1948, in Casper, Wyoming. His father, Orin Wesley Coburn, was an optician and founder of Coburn Optical Industries. Tom Coburn attended the O. W. Coburn School of Law, which was named after his father and was a part of Oral Roberts University.

Coburn began his political career in 1994 when he was elected to the U.S. House of Representatives as part of the Republican Revolution. He upheld his campaign pledge to serve no more than three consecutive terms and did not run for re-election in 2000. In 2004, he returned to political life with a successful run for the U.S. Senate. Coburn was re-elected to a second term in 2010 and pledged not to seek a third term.

After leaving Congress, Coburn worked with the Manhattan Institute for Policy Research on its efforts to reform the Food and Drug Administration, becoming a senior fellow of the institute in December 2016. He also serves as a senior advisor to Citizens for Self-Governance, where he has been active in calling for a convention to propose amendments to the United States Constitution.

Throughout his political career, Coburn earned a reputation for his use of the Senate hold privilege to prevent several bills from coming to the Senate floor. In November 2009, he drew attention for placing a hold on a veterans benefits bill known as the Veterans' Caregiver and Omnibus Health Benefits Act.

Coburn's health began to decline, and he announced in 2014 that he would be retiring at the end of the year. During his time in the Senate, he introduced the Insurance Capital Standards Clarification Act of 2014, which passed in June 2014. Coburn also made headlines for a bet he made with Florida Senator Bill Nelson over a football game between the University of Oklahoma and the University of Florida. The loser had to serenade the winner with a song, and Coburn sang Elton John's "Rocket Man" to Nelson, who had once flown into space.

question: Question: Tell me a bio of Lennie Hayton.
answer:
Lennie Hayton was an American musician, composer, conductor, and arranger, born on February 14, 1908, in New York City to a Jewish family. His father was a Manhattan restaurateur, and he developed an early interest in music, particularly the early classics, at the age of six, inspired by the rolls of the family player piano.

Hayton began his career working with Bing Crosby, providing musical support for his theatre appearances and radio shows. They toured together, including a tour of Paramount-Publix theatres, and Hayton also recorded with Crosby, achieving hits with songs like "Cabin in the Cotton", "Love Me Tonight", and "Some of These Days".

In 1940, Hayton became a musical director for Metro-Goldwyn-Mayer (MGM) and guided the studio through its prime years as a forerunner of the movie musical. He was nominated for four Academy Awards during his tenure at MGM, winning one for the music of "On the Town" in 1950. He also arranged the music for "Singin' in the Rain" in 1952.

Hayton married Lena Horne in December 1947 in Paris. Throughout their marriage, Hayton also acted as Horne's music director. However, the marriage was tumultuous due to the stresses and pressures of an interracial relationship, which was still relatively rare in that time period. They were separated for most of the 1960s.

Hayton was a heavy drinker and smoker and died of heart disease while separated from Horne, in Palm Springs, California in 1971. He was buried in the Hollywood Forever Cemetery in Hollywood, California. His trademark was the wearing of a captain's hat, which he always wore at a rakish angle.

Before marrying Horne, Hayton was married to Helen Maude Gifford, who died in 1943. He also co-arranged the Hoagy Carmichael composition "Stardust" with Artie Shaw, for Shaw's recording of it in 1940.

Jean Muir (actress) was an American stage and film actress and educator, born on February 13, 1911, in Suffern, New York. She was the first performer to be blacklisted after her name appeared in the infamous anti-Communist 1950 pamphlet "Red Channels". Her parents were a certified public accountant and a substitute teacher.

Muir made her Broadway debut in "The Truth Game" in 1930 and was later signed by Warner Bros., with whom she made 14 films. In 1940, she married attorney Henry Jaffe and they had three children.

In the mid-1950s, Muir reportedly suffered from alcoholism and cirrhosis of the liver. She died in a nursing home in Mesa, Arizona on July 23, 1996. Muir has a star on the Hollywood Walk of Fame at 6280 Hollywood Blvd.

Shortly before her death, Muir began fundraising for the National Museum of Scotland in Edinburgh. Her husband and Jean Muir Ltd. continued this work in her memory, as did many of her personal friends and loyal customers. The Museum's Silver Room is dedicated to Jean Muir, while Jean Muir Ltd is named upon the founder's stone at the Museum entrance.

question: Question: Tell me a bio of Alexander Vovin.
answer:
Alexander Vovin is a Russian-American linguist and philologist, currently serving as directeur d'études at the School for Advanced Studies in the Social Sciences (École des hautes études en sciences sociales (EHESS)) in Paris, France. He was born in Saint Petersburg, Russia, in 1961.

Vovin earned his M.A. in structural and applied linguistics from the Saint Petersburg State University in 1983, and his Ph.D. in historical Japanese linguistics and premodern Japanese literature from the same university in 1987, with a doctoral dissertation on the "Hamamatsu Chūnagon Monogatari" (ca. 1056).

His research interests include etymology, morphology, and phonology of Japanese, the philology of the Nara period (710–792), and to a lesser extent of the Heian period (792–1192). He is currently working on the complete academic translation into English of the Man'yōshū (ca. 759), the earliest and the largest premodern Japanese poetic anthology, alongside the critical edition of the original text and commentaries.

In addition to his work on Japanese, Vovin has researched the moribund Ainu language in northern Japan, and worked on Inner Asian languages and Kra–Dai languages, especially those preserved only in Chinese transcription, as well as on Old and Middle Korean texts.

Vovin has also made significant contributions to the classification of the Japonic languages. He reconstructed the morphology of Proto-Japanese and found many similarities between Proto-Japanese and several Southeast-Asian languages. He proposed that the location of the Japonic Urheimat (linguistic homeland) is in Southern China.

In terms of his work on other languages, Vovin deciphered the Brahmi script of the Inscription of Hüis Tolgoi found in Bulgan Province, Mongolia, and analyzed its language, finding similarities to Middle Mongolian as opposed to the more southern Khitan language.

Overall, Alexander Vovin is a renowned linguist with a wide range of expertise in various languages and periods, particularly in Japanese

question: Question: Tell me a bio of Dana Awartani.
answer:
Dana Awartani is a Palestinian-Saudi artist born in 1987 in Jeddah, Saudi Arabia, where she currently resides and works. She received her bachelor's degree in Fine Art from Central Saint Martins in London and later obtained a Master's in Traditional Arts from the Princes School in London. At the Prince’s School, she learned various traditional techniques from cultures worldwide, including stained glass, miniature painting, gilding, and more. However, she couldn't study illumination there, so she found a master in Turkey to help her master this technique.

Dana Awartani's work is unique as it incorporates traditional methods of Islamic art into a contemporary context. Her work is rich in geometric patterning and intricate details, often integrating the patterning styles of Islamic art. She specializes in geometry, illumination, tile-work, and parquetry. Her work explores the relationship between geometry and nature, as well as how truths can be translated through art using geometric principles, visualizing a sacred language through a symbolic and multi-layered aesthetic.

Behind every structured piece, Dana Awartani emphasizes that there is no randomness. She considers Islamic Art as a sacred spiritual practice used for worshiping God and for God. For her, creating art is a form of prayer and dhikr (remembrance). She needs to be in a good mood and fully focused to be able to create her work, as otherwise, it doesn't work.

Dana Awartani's work has been practiced, although less and less, as a substitute for the forbidden depiction of divine figures. She believes that as Arabs, they are surrounded by this fine art but are often unaware of it. She discovered her yearning for it and found an inner and outer beauty behind it, telling a story.

question: Question: Tell me a bio of Jake Tilson.
answer:
Jake Tilson is an English artist, graphic designer, writer, and publisher, born on February 14, 1958, in London. He is the son of Joe Tilson and Joslyn Tilson (née Morton). His grandfather, Alastair Morton, ran his father's business, the Edinburgh Weavers, commissioning artists such as Ben Nicholson and Barbara Hepworth.

Tilson studied painting at Chelsea School of Art from 1976–79, and at the Royal College of Art from 1980–83. He won the Royal College of Art Major Travelling scholarship and spent a year working in Paris, where he had his first one-person exhibition at Galerie J et J Donguy.

In 1979, he set up the small independent press, The Woolley Dale Press, which enabled him to publish his works. He is known for his playful, multilayered work that defies both convention and easy description. His practice spans publishing, cultural commentary, photography, and audio work, often focusing on the unremarkable and the everyday while purposefully avoiding any sense of spectacle.

Tilson has produced work for companies such as Paul Smith, Haworth Tompkins, Royal National Theatre, and Warehouse plc. He is a trustee of the Oxford Symposium on Food & Cookery. He has also taught in the Communication Design department at the Royal College of Art and worked as a journalist.

His works have been exhibited in various places, including a retrospective exhibition at the Museo Internacional de Electrografia in Cuenca, Spain, part-funded by The British Council. He has also published several books, including "A Tale of 12 Kitchens" and "In At The Deep End" – cooking fish Tokyo to Venice.

Tilson is married and has three children. He continues to live and work in London and Italy. His work can be found in collections such as the Tate Gallery Collection, Chase Manhattan Bank, Arthur Andersen & Co., BBC World Service, The Principal Financial Group, USA, among others.

question: Question: Tell me a bio of Worranit Thawornwong.
answer:
Worranit Thawornwong, better known as Mook, is a Thai actress and singer. She was born on 9 October 1996 in Bangkok, Thailand, and is the second child in her family. Her brother, Jirakit Thawornwong, is also an actor. She attended high school at Satriwitthaya 2 School and is currently studying at Kasetsart University.

Worranit started her acting career in 2014 through Channel Bang for the drama "Rukjing Pinker" as Bew. She gained significant popularity through the 2015 Thai television series "Ugly Duckling Series: Perfect Match," where she played the character Junior. Notable dramas she has starred in include "Mah Tun Welah Por Dee," "Kon Jao Choo" ("Bee Dup Bee Doo") for Ugly Duckling: Perfect Match, and "Poot Wah Ruk Nai Jai" for Roon Pee Secret Love.

In addition to acting, Worranit has also sung a few songs for various dramas, including a song for Ugly Duckling: Perfect Match. She has participated in several other dramas, such as Kiss The Series, U-Prince, My Dear Loser, and Monster Romance.

Worranit has also worked with other notable Thai actors, such as Perawat Sangpotirat, with whom she starred in the show "Mint To Be." This show was popular not only in Thailand but also in China, where it was simultaneously telecasted on Tencent and garnered massive views in a short time, making it one of the hottest Thai dramas in China.

question: Question: Tell me a bio of Vanda Pignato.
answer:
Vanda Pignato is a Brazilian-born Salvadoran lawyer, human rights activist, politician, women's rights activist, and former First Lady of El Salvador. She was born on February 16, 1963. Pignato served as First Lady of El Salvador from June 1, 2009, when her husband, President Mauricio Funes, appointed her as the country's Secretary of Social Inclusion, a position she held until 2014. This made Pignato the first sitting First Lady in El Salvador's history to hold a political position.

Funes's successor, President Salvador Sánchez Cerén, reappointed Pignato as Secretary of Social Inclusion when he took office. In this role, Pignato oversaw issues related to human rights and family affairs in El Salvador.

Pignato has been a strong advocate for women's rights and gender equality. She has acknowledged the challenges facing Salvadoran women, who have higher high school dropout rates and lower literacy rates than men.

In October 2014, Mauricio Funes publicly confirmed that he and Pignato had separated. In July 2015, Pignato announced that she had been diagnosed with cancer and took a temporary leave of absence from the Department of Social Inclusion to undergo treatment for the disease.

In June 2018, a warrant was issued for Pignato's arrest in connection with a case against former President Mauricio Funes for the crimes of embezzlement, and money and asset laundering. However, the judge decided to issue a warrant despite a request for Pignato to only pay a bond to be processed in freedom as a consideration for her health condition.

question: Question: Tell me a bio of Iggy Azalea.

In 2013, Azalea released her debut single as a lead artist, "Work," from her debut studio album, "The New Classic," which was released in 2014. "Work" was developed with motivational and inspirational intentions to portray her life story, specifically dealing with her struggle as an up-and-coming rapper and her relocation from Australia.

Azalea's debut album peaked inside the top five on the record charts of countries including the United States. In late 2014, she was placed at number-one on "Billboard" Year-End's Top New Artists chart. In 2015, Azalea led the 2015 iHeartRadio Music Awards nominations with five and received twelve nominations at the 2015 "Billboard" Music Awards. In 2016, Azalea was presented with the Woman of the Year award by GQ Australia.

Azalea has also collaborated with other artists, such as Britney Spears on the single "Pretty Girls," which was released in 2015. Overall, Azalea has released one studio album, four extended plays (EPs), two mixtapes, and 16 singles (including four as a featured artist).

question: Question: Tell me a bio of Feroze Gandhi.
answer:
Feroze Gandhi was an Indian politician and journalist, born on September 12, 1912, to a Parsi family. He served as the publisher of "The National Herald" and "The Navjivan" newspapers from Lucknow. In 1942, he married Indira Nehru, the daughter of Jawaharlal Nehru, and they had two sons, Rajiv and Sanjay. His elder son, Rajiv, later became the Prime Minister of India.

Feroze Gandhi served as a member of the provincial parliament from 1950 to 1952, and later a member of the Lok Sabha, the Lower House of India's parliament. He helped found a college in Rae Bareli, which was named after him.

In 1952, after Feroze Gandhi was elected to Parliament, he moved to Delhi, where he was assigned an MP quarters. However, his wife Indira continued to stay with her father, Jawaharlal Nehru, putting a final seal on their separation.

Feroze Gandhi passed away on September 8, 1960. A thermal power plant in Unchahar, Raebareli district, Uttar Pradesh, was later renamed Feroze Gandhi Unchahar Thermal Power Plant in his honor. Additionally, an engineering college in Raebareli, Uttar Pradesh, was named Feroze Gandhi Institute of Engineering and Technology.

question: Question: Tell me a bio of Thomas Piketty.
answer:
Thomas Piketty is a French economist, born on May 7, 1971, in the Parisian suburb of Clichy, Hauts-de-Seine. He is currently a professor (directeur d'études) at the School for Advanced Studies in the Social Sciences (EHESS), associate chair at the Paris School of Economics, and Centennial professor at the International Inequalities Institute, which is part of the London School of Economics (LSE).

Piketty's work primarily focuses on wealth and income inequality. He gained significant attention with his best-selling book "Capital in the Twenty-First Century" (2013), which emphasizes the themes of wealth concentrations and distribution over the past 250 years. The book argues that the rate of return on capital in developed countries is persistently greater than the rate of economic growth, and this will cause wealth inequality to increase in the future.

To address this issue, Piketty proposes redistribution through a progressive global tax on wealth. He has long-standing ties to the London School of Economics, having completed his PhD studies at the university in the early 1990s. He joined the LSE in 2015 as the distinguished Centennial Professor and continues his research as part of the LSE International Inequalities Institute.

In addition to his research, Piketty also teaches post-graduate students at the LSE. He has served as an economic advisor to the Socialist Party and has been a columnist for the French newspaper "Libération" and occasionally writes op-eds for "Le Monde". However, it's important to note that in 2009, he was accused of domestic violence by his partner, Aurélie Filippetti, which he acknowledged and apologized for, following which she withdrew her complaint.

question: Question: Tell me a bio of Vladimir Lenin.
answer:
Vladimir Ilyich Lenin was a Russian revolutionary, politician, and political theorist who is best known for his role as the leader of the Bolshevik Party and the Soviet Union's first head of government. He was born on April 22, 1870, in Simbirsk, Russia, and died on January 21, 1924, in Gorki, Russia.

Lenin's political career began in the late 19th century when he became involved in the Russian Social Democratic Labor Party. He was exiled several times for his political activities, but he continued to advocate for socialist revolution. In 1903, he helped found the Bolshevik faction of the Russian Social Democratic Labor Party, which later became the Communist Party of the Soviet Union.

Lenin played a key role in the Russian Revolution of 1917, which led to the overthrow of the Russian monarchy and the establishment of a provisional government. He then led the Bolsheviks in the October Revolution, which established the Soviet Union. Lenin served as the first head of government of the Soviet Union, holding the position of Chairman of the Council of People's Commissars from 1917 to 1924.

Lenin's political ideas and policies had a significant impact on the Soviet Union and the world. He is often credited with developing the theory of "democratic centralism," which emphasized the importance of democratic decision-making at the local level while also requiring strict obedience to centralized leadership. He also played a key role in the establishment of the Communist International, an organization designed to promote communist revolution around the world.

Lenin's legacy is complex and controversial. While he is often celebrated as a hero of the working class and a champion of socialist revolution, he is also criticized for his authoritarianism and his role in the suppression of political dissent. He is remembered as a key figure in the history of the Soviet Union and the modern world.

There are many monuments dedicated to Lenin, including the Vladimir Lenin monument in Azov, Russia, which was opened in 1978. There is also a statue of Lenin in Kiev, Ukraine, which was toppled during the Euromaidan protests in 2013.
