question: Question: Tell me a bio of Carol Dweck.
answer:
Carol S. Dweck is the Lewis and Virginia Eaton Professor of Psychology at Stanford University, known for her work on the mindset psychological trait. Born on October 17, 1946, in New York, Dweck is the middle sibling of three children. Her father worked in export-import and her mother in advertising.

Dweck taught at Columbia University, Harvard University, and the University of Illinois before joining the Stanford University faculty in 2004. She is married to David Goldman, a national theatre director and critic, and the founder and director of the National Center for New Plays at Stanford University. Although she did not have children of her own, her husband has two grown children, whom the grandchildren call Dweck "grandma."

In September 2017, Dweck won the biggest prize in education circles, $3.8 million to continue her research on the ability to learn. She maintains a teaching presence as a psychology professor at Stanford for the 2017-18 school year, teaching Developmental Psychology, Self Theories, and Independent Studies.

Dweck's work focuses on the impact of mindset on motivation and performance. She maintains that the belief in one's ability to learn and grow, known as a growth mindset, is crucial for personal freedom and equality. Dweck is an elected member of the American Academy of Arts & Sciences.

In response to criticisms, Dweck has shown openness and willingness to address problems, as demonstrated when Nick Brown found inconsistencies in her work and she acknowledged and addressed them. Despite some skepticism about mindset as a construct, Brown praised Dweck's dedication to doing thorough research.

question: Question: Tell me a bio of Ruth Fischer.
answer:
Ruth Fischer was an Austrian and German Communist who was born on December 11, 1895, in Leipzig, Germany. She was the daughter of Marie Edith Fischer and Rudolf Eisler, a professor of philosophy. Fischer was of Jewish father and Lutheran mother heritage. She was the elder sister to noted film composer Hanns Eisler and Communist activist Ruth Fischer.

Fischer co-founded the Austrian Communist Party in 1918. Later, she married fellow communist Gustav Golke in order to be naturalized as a German. In the early months of 1923, she and Arkadi Maslow urged the national leader of the Communist Party of Germany, Heinrich Brandler, to organize an uprising on the model provided by the Bolsheviks in 1917. They developed the "theory of the offensive."

Fischer denounced the leadership for "making concessions to social democracy," for "opportunism," and for "ideological liquidationism and theoretical revisionism." In 1923, she appealed to a group of Nazi students, proclaiming that "Those who call for a struggle against Jewish capital are already, gentlemen, class strugglers, even if they don’t know it."

In the later years, Fischer became a staunch anti-Communist activist and, according to secret information declassified in 2010, was a key agent of the American intelligence service known as "The Pond." She returned to Paris in 1955 and published her books "Stalin and German Communism" and "Die Umformung der Sowjetgesellschaft." Fischer died in Paris in 1961, aged 65, from undisclosed causes. She had one child, Friedrich Gerhart Friedländer (F.G. Friedlander), born in Vienna in 1917, who later became a mathematician and died in the United Kingdom in 2001. The International Institute of Social History has an archive of her papers.

question: Question: Tell me a bio of Asafa Powell.
answer:
Asafa Powell, CD, born on November 23, 1982, is a Jamaican sprinter who specializes in the 100 meters. He is a past student of Charlemont High School in Jamaica, and there has been a proposal to rename the school to the Asafa Powell High School in his honor. However, this proposal has faced opposition from the Charlemont High School Past Students.

Powell held the 100 meters world record between June 2005 and May 2008, with times of 9.77 and 9.74 seconds. He has consistently broken the 10-second barrier in competition, with his personal best of 9.72 s ranks fourth on the all-time list of male 100 meter athletes. As of September 1, 2016, Powell has broken the ten-second barrier more times than anyone else – 97 times. He currently holds the world record for the 100 yard dash.

Powell has competed in the World Athletics Championships seven times, winning the 100 m four times and the 200 m once. In total, he has won $173,000 in prize money in the male events.

Powell is deeply religious and cites his mother and father and his strict upbringing as the reason for this. He has faced personal tragedy, with the deaths of two of his brothers. In 2002, one of his brothers, Michael Powell, was shot dead in a taxi in New York. This emotional event happened the week of the Jamaica National Trials. In 2003, Asafa lost another brother during the week of the Jamaica National Championships.

Powell is an avid car enthusiast and is good friends with compatriot, 100 and 200 metre world record holder Usain Bolt. The two are often seen joking around and do meet off the track. Powell is known to be occasionally shy but nonetheless good natured and somewhat of a joker. He has also released an apparel line.

Warfa was a professor at the Somali National University, where he taught biology and agriculture. In 1994, Warfa survived an assassination attempt in which he was shot at a checkpoint. After this incident, he left Somalia for Nairobi, Kenya. He then emigrated to the United States and joined Salt Lake Community College as a volunteer professor and worked at Brigham Young University as a professor of biology.

He continues to attend conferences on herbology as a keynote speaker or contributor. He is rumored to have a past supercar collection of over $15 million and a current watch collection of $5 million as of late 2016.

Warfa is currently writing an autobiography and was a candidate for president of Somalia in 2012. His work continues to be celebrated and admired, with many of his designs still standing today. Antonio Leviste, born on January 14, 1940, is a Filipino politician and businessman. He hails from a distinguished Batangueño family known for their involvement in both business and politics. Leviste served as the Governor of Batangas from 1972 to 1980.

In his personal life, he was married to Senator Loren Legarda, but they separated before the 2004 election campaign. Their marriage produced two sons, Lorenzo "Lanz" Leviste and Leandro "Lean" Leviste.

Leviste is also the father of Toni Leviste, who is a practicing Muslim and an equestrienne. Toni opened a 5-hectare Equestrian park in Lipa city, Batangas.

In his professional career, Leviste is a Lt. Commander in the Philippine Navy Reserve Force and is the Honorary Consul General of the State of Palestine. He is the charter president of the Resort Association of the Philippines and co-founder of the Tourism Council of the Philippines. Leviste is the chief executive officer of the Leviste Group of Companies, a real estate firm engaged in housing, subdivision, condominium, and resort development.

answer:

In January 2001, he transferred to Venezia, and then to Palermo, as Maurizio Zamparini, owner of Venezia, bought Palermo. He was also on loan to U.S. Lecce.

In 2003, Rossi was signed by Siena. However, he was banned from football due to a betting scandal in 2004. He then signed an 18-month contract with Queens Park Rangers in January 2005. In summer 2005, he was signed by Triestina. In January 2008, he was on loan to Calcio Catania, with Babu moving in the opposite direction. Rossi became the third choice goalkeeper at Catania, behind Ciro Polito and Albano Bizarri, and was ahead of Raffaele Ioime.

During the 2008/2009 season, Rossi was transferred to Gallipoli in Lega Pro Prima Divisione – B. Although the club won Serie B promotion, the team faced financial difficulty, and Rossi left the club. In February 2010, Rossi was signed by Sorrento. Rossi spent the next two and a half seasons at Sorrento and became an integral member of the team that twice nearly gained promotion to Serie B.

In summer 2012, after the resignation of Sorrento's president and much speculation as to whether the club would continue, Rossi left Sorrento to seek employment elsewhere. question: Question: Tell me a bio of Yehuda Lindell.
answer:
Yehuda Lindell is a professor in the Department of Computer Science at Bar-Ilan University, where he conducts research on cryptography with a focus on the theory of secure computation and its application in practice. He was born on February 24, 1971.

Lindell received his BSc and MSc degrees in computer science from Bar-Ilan University. He then obtained a PhD in computer science from the Weizmann Institute of Science in 2002. After completing his education, he spent two years at IBM's cryptography research group at the T.J. Watson Research Center, where he received a Raviv Fellowship.

Lindell's work on secure computation was recognized by the award of an ERC starting grant in 2009 and an ERC consolidators grant in 2014. He worked as a permanent cryptographic consultant to Safenet from 2004 to 2014. Since 2014, he is the co-founder and chief scientist of Unbound Tech (formerly, Dyadic Security).

Lindell's main contributions focus on the examination of the Yao garbled circuit construction. His most cited work is a joint paper with Benny Pinkas on privacy preserving data mining in which the use of secure computation was proposed for performing data mining algorithms. He is also the author of a textbook with Jonathan Katz on modern cryptography, which is utilized in many universities around the world as a standard reference work.

question: Question: Tell me a bio of Zewde Gebre-Sellassie.
answer:
Zewde Gebre-Sellassie was a prominent nobleman, historian, and former deputy Prime Minister of Ethiopia. He was born on October 12, 1926, in the village of Galdu, to the north-west of Addis Ababa. His father was "Dejazmatch" Gebre Selassie Baria Gabr, the governor of Adwa, and his mother was "Leult" Wolete Israel Seyoum.

Zewde received his initial education in Addis Ababa under a tutor. Later, he went to school in Jerusalem and Cairo, where his mother stayed during the Fascist occupation of Ethiopia. After the liberation, he enrolled at the Haile Selassie I secondary school in Addis Ababa and subsequently joined the University of Exeter, England, where he studied English literature. He then pursued legal training at St. Anthony's College, Oxford, where he became a senior member from 1963 to 1971. After completing his studies, he was called to the Bar, Lincoln's Inn, London.

Throughout his career, Zewde held various public offices in Ethiopia, including that of deputy prime minister. Under the imperial government, he held several positions. However, in November 1974, the Provisional Military Administrative Council's (Derg) summary execution of high government officials of the previous regime forced him into exile. He eventually became vice-president of the United Nations Economic and Social Council and worked for several years as an advisor to the secretariat of the United Nations.

Zewde harmoniously combined oral tradition with profound western education and readily availed of them to any academic who sought his assistance. He was known for his immense popularity among all walks of life. His funeral was attended by a huge crowd of mourners, and a week-long exhibition of his works and photos was held in his memory at the main campus of Addis Ababa University.

Zewde passed away on December 15, 2008, in Addis Ababa. Scholars of African history often compared the passing away of a knowledgeable person like Zewde to a library consumed by conflagration. He received national honors throughout his service.

question: Question: Tell me a bio of Patoranking.
answer:
Patoranking, whose real name is Patoranking Patrick Nnaemeka Okorie, is a Nigerian reggae-dancehall singer and songwriter. He was born on May 27, 1990, in Ijegun-Egba, and hails from Onicha in Ebonyi State. Patoranking started his musical career doing underground collaborations with artists such as XProject, Konga, Slam, and Reggie Rockstone. He signed a record deal with K-Solo's Igberaga Records in 2010, releasing "Up in D Club" under the outfit.

Patoranking became a protégé of Dem Mama Records after collaborating with Timaya on his song "Alubarika". In February 2014, he signed a record deal with Foston Musik. In February 2014, Patoranking released "Girlie O", a song produced by WizzyPro, which put him in the limelight. He also announced via Instagram that he signed a distribution deal with VP Records around the same time.

Patoranking has had several successes in his career. In 2016, he released his debut studio album, "God Over Everything", which debuted at No. 4 on Billboard's Reggae Albums chart. The album features guest appearances from Phyno, Wizkid, Sarkodie, Olamide, Elephant Man, and Wasiu Ayinde Marshall.

In January 2016, Patoranking was announced as one of the judges for the maiden edition of the singing competition "The Voice Nigeria". He has also been involved in mentoring upcoming artists, such as Chike, a contestant on "The Voice Nigeria" who chose to be on Team Patoranking.

Patoranking started his performing arts career as a street jam and carnival dancer before transitioning into music. He has been recognized for his talent and potential by industry veterans, such as Timaya and James Arthur, who have praised him and expressed their belief in his ability to become a superstar.

answer:
James Theodore Bent (March 30, 1852 – May 5, 1897) was an English explorer, archaeologist, and author. He was born in Baildon House, near Bradford, Yorkshire, and was educated at Repton School and Wadham College, Oxford, where he graduated in 1875. In 1877, he married Mabel, daughter of R. W. Hall-Dare of Newtownbarry, Co. Wexford, and she became his companion in all his travels.

Bent went abroad every year and became thoroughly acquainted with Italy and Greece. In 1879, he published a book on the republic of Venice. His interest in archaeology led him to the Bahrein Islands of the Persian Gulf, where he found evidence of a primitive home of the Phoenician civilization.

In 1890, Bent embarked on an expedition to Cilicia Trachea, where he obtained a valuable collection of inscriptions. The following year, he spent a year in South Africa, investigating some of the ruins in Mashonaland to shed light on the origin and early history of East Africa. He made the first detailed examination of the Great Zimbabwe and described his work in "The Ruined Cities of Mashonaland" (1892).

In 1893, Bent investigated the ruins of a very ancient gold-mine on the African coast of the Red Sea, finding there traces of what he considered Sabean influence. However, his theories about the Semitic origin of the ruins in Mashonaland have not been accepted by archaeologists.

While on another journey in South Arabia and Socotra (1896–1897), Bent was seized with malarial fever and died in London on May 5, 1897, a few days after his return. Mabel, who had contributed by her skill as a photographer and in other ways to the success of her husband's journeys, published in 1900 "Southern Arabia, Soudan and Sakotra", which she recorded the results of their last expedition into those regions.

answer:

He began his professional MMA career in 2010, fighting in various promotions such as Cage Warriors, ProFC, Fight Nights (EFN), and others before joining the Ultimate Fighting Championship (UFC) in 2014.

Tukhugov made his UFC debut in 2015, but his first scheduled fight against Thiago Tavares was scrapped due to a rib injury. He later faced and defeated Douglas Silva de Andrade in his debut. Tukhugov also won against Phillipe Nover by split decision in December 2015.

In a controversial fight against Renato Moicano in May 2016, Tukhugov suffered two kicks to the groin, but the referee allowed the fight to continue. Despite this, he lost the fight via split decision. Tukhugov was pulled from a fight in December 2016 after being notified by USADA for an undisclosed reason.

In October 2018, Tukhugov was involved in a post-fight brawl at UFC 229, where he was one of Khabib Nurmagomedov's cornermen who attacked Conor McGregor and his cornermen. This incident led to Tukhugov being released from the UFC. Prior to this incident, Tukhugov had received a USADA suspension in 2016 for illegally using performance enhancing drugs.

question: Question: Tell me a bio of Belisarius.
answer:
Belisarius was a general of the Byzantine Empire, living from around 500 to 565. He is a significant figure in history, particularly known for his role in Emperor Justinian's ambitious project of reconquering much of the Mediterranean territory.

In the early 530s, Belisarius took a Thracian named Theodosius under his protection, treating him as an adoptive son, though not legally adopting him. This relationship became a subject of controversy, as it is said that an affair between Antonina, Belisarius' wife, and Theodosius blossomed during the Vandalic War and continued in the Gothic War. This affair was apparently common knowledge among Belisarius' staff, yet Belisarius was reportedly unaware of it at first.

Belisarius' military exploits are well-documented. He played a crucial role in the Byzantine conquest of the Vandal Kingdom in North Africa, culminating in the capture of Carthage. Afterwards, Justinian recalled Belisarius and sent him to Italy, where he successfully invaded and put down dynastic squabbles among the Ostrogoths.

However, Belisarius' personal life and character have been subject to various interpretations. Procopius, his secretary, portrayed him as a cuckold husband and a love-blind fool in his historical treatise, the "Secret History". This work is an extended attack on Belisarius and Antonina, and on Justinian and Theodora. Other authors, such as Graves in his historical novel "Count Belisarius", present Belisarius as a general hampered by his rigid code of honor and loyalty to his Emperor.

Despite the controversies surrounding his personal life, Belisarius' military achievements have secured him a place in history as one of the Byzantine Empire's most successful generals.

question: Question: Tell me a bio of Andry Rajoelina.
answer:
Andry Rajoelina was born on May 30, 1974, in Antsirabe, Madagascar, to a relatively wealthy family. His father, Roger Yves Rajoelina, was a retired colonel who held dual nationality and fought for the French army in the Algerian War. Despite having the means for a college education, Andry Rajoelina chose to discontinue his studies after completing his baccalauréat to pursue a career as an entrepreneur.

In 1994, Rajoelina met his future spouse. He gained prominence in 2009 when he led the opposition against President Ravalomanana. On January 17, 2009, he gathered 30,000 supporters at a public park, which he renamed "Place de la Démocratie," to defy the public executive power of Ravalomanana. On January 31, 2009, he announced that he was taking control of the country's affairs, declaring: "Since the president and the government have not assumed their responsibilities, I therefore proclaim that I will run all national affairs as of today."

Rajoelina's self-declaration of power discredited his democratic aims, and the number of attendees at subsequent rallies declined, averaging around 3,000 to 5,000 participants. On February 3, 2009, the Ministry of Domestic Affairs dismissed Rajoelina as mayor of Antananarivo and appointed a special delegation to manage the affairs of the capital. Rajoelina contested the decision.

In December 2011, Rajoelina was officially received by the French President Nicolas Sarkozy. In May 2013, when Ravalonana's wife announced her candidacy for the 2013 elections, Rajoelina saw it as a breach of contract and reintroduced his own candidacy for the elections. This situation led to the postponement of the election dates multiple times. A special electoral court ruled in August 2013 that the candidatures of Rajoelina, Ravalomanana, and Ratsiraka were invalid and not permitted to run in the 2013 election.

question: Question: Tell me a bio of Alf Garland.
answer:
Alf Garland was an Australian Army officer and a prominent figure in military and political circles. He was born on March 19, 1932, and passed away on March 9, 2002, after a long battle with motor neurone disease. Garland served in the Australian Army for 35 years, during which he commanded the 1st Special Air Service squadron against Indonesian forces in Borneo in 1965 and was second-in-command of the 7th Battalion, Royal Australian Regiment, during the Vietnam War. He was also appointed Australia's chief liaison officer to US forces.

Garland was the National President of the Returned and Services League of Australia (RSL) from 1988 to 1993. He was also the President of the Australian Capital Territory branch of the RSL before becoming the National President. In 1988, he was elected as the Australian Monarchist League delegate from New South Wales at the 1998 Australian Constitutional Convention. He joined Bruce Ruxton in campaigning against the notion of Australia becoming a republic.

Garland was known for his outspokenness on controversial social issues and often antagonised the Keating government at the time. He was Chairman of both the New South Wales and ACT branches of the Australian Monarchist League. In one attempt to filibuster debate at the 1998 Australian Constitutional Convention, Garland recounted his family's loyalty to the Crown beginning in medieval times.

Garland attracted media attention throughout his career and was a controversial figure due to his outspokenness on various issues. He died at the age of 69.

question: Question: Tell me a bio of Jeremy Corbyn.
answer:
Jeremy Corbyn is a British politician who has served as the Leader of the Opposition and Leader of the Labour Party since 2015. He represents the constituency of Islington North in the House of Commons, a position he has held since 1983.

Corbyn's political career began in the 1970s, and he has been a long-serving backbench MP. His rise to leadership of the Labour Party was unexpected and is analyzed in the book "Jeremy Corbyn: Accidental Hero" by W Stephen Gilbert. The book evaluates Corbyn's life, career, and future as Labour leader.

Corbyn's leadership of the Labour Party began in September 2015, following the resignation of Ed Miliband in the wake of Labour's defeat at the 2015 general election. He faced a second leadership election in 2016, but was re-elected.

Corbyn's leadership has been marked by a focus on left-wing policies, and he has faced criticism for his allegedly weak support for the Remain campaign in the referendum on membership of the European Union. However, he has also gained support from younger voters, with poll data showing that 61.5% of under-40s voted for Labour in the 2017 general election.

Following the general election result, Labour Party membership increased by 35,000 within four days. Many senior Labour MPs and former advisers who have previously criticized Corbyn expressed notably different attitudes towards him after Theresa May was prevented from obtaining the majority she sought in the election.

The book "Jeremy Corbyn: Accidental Hero" has been praised for its informative and thoughtful analysis of Corbyn's rise to leadership and his politics. It has been described as a "highly readable and comprehensible introduction" to Corbyn and his politics.

question: Question: Tell me a bio of Jefferson Thomas.
answer:
Thomas Jefferson was an American Founding Father, born on April 13, 1743 (April 2, according to the Julian calendar in use at the time) and passed away on July 4, 1826. He played a significant role in the establishment of the United States, serving as the principal author of the Declaration of Independence and as the third President of the United States from 1801 to 1809.

Jefferson's life and work are extensively documented, particularly through the scholarly edition known as The Papers of Thomas Jefferson. This multi-volume project, established at Princeton University, is the definitive edition of documents written by or to Jefferson, covering his public and private papers from his entire life.

Jefferson's plantation, Monticello, is another important source of information about his life. The Thomas Jefferson Foundation, which manages Monticello, has published several books on Jefferson's history, nature, science, and friendship with James Monroe, among other topics. The Foundation also houses the Robert H. Smith International Center for Jefferson Studies, a scholarly hub dedicated to fostering Thomas Jefferson scholarship and disseminating findings through research and education.

In the realm of healthcare, Jefferson's legacy lives on through Thomas Jefferson University and its associated hospitals, such as Thomas Jefferson University Hospital, Jefferson Hospital for Neuroscience, and Jefferson Methodist Hospital. These institutions serve patients in Philadelphia and the surrounding communities in the Delaware Valley.

Jefferson's influence extends beyond the United States, as well. In Washington, D.C., a memorial dedicated to him was established in 1943, on the 200th anniversary of his birth. The memorial features a statue of Jefferson and engravings of passages from his writings, most prominently the words inscribed around the monument: "I have sworn upon the altar of God eternal hostility against every form of tyranny over the mind of man."

In summary, Thomas Jefferson was a key figure in the founding of the United States, and his life, ideas, and contributions continue to be studied and celebrated today.

Fifi Cooper is known for her unpredictable, punchy, and hearty rapping style. She has collaborated with several artists, including Khuli Chana, AKA, and Mo'Molemi. She is a single mother and has a son named Resego.

Despite her diagnosis, she continued to perform until late 2004. In 1989, at the age of 22, she formed an edgy girl group called "Minako with Wild Cats". However, by 1992, she reinvented herself, taking formal acting and singing lessons, and became a notable theatrical singer and actress.

In her career, Honda was cast in various stage plays. In 2005, she was originally cast as Fantine in Les Misérables for the Japanese tour, but due to her death, another actor was given the part. She was also set to star in the stage play "Minako-taiyo ni Natta Utahime", but this was after her diagnosis and before her death.

Honda had a relapse after celebrating her 38th birthday at home and suffered from lung complications. She received treatment, including a dose of anticancer medicine from the United States, but unfortunately, she passed away at the Juntendo University Hospital in Bunkyō, Tokyo, on November 6, 2005, officially from acute myelogenous leukemia. She was 38 and unmarried at the time of her death.

question: Question: Tell me a bio of Richard Kuklinski.
answer:
Richard Leonard Kuklinski, also known as "The Iceman," was an American hitman and serial killer born on April 11, 1935, and passed away on March 5, 2006. He was associated with various Mafia groups, including the DeCavalcante crime family of Newark, New Jersey, and the Five Families of New York City.

Kuklinski was given the nickname "The Iceman" due to his method of freezing a victim to mask the time of death. He was convicted of murdering six people, but confessed to and is suspected of far more murders.

In 1985, Detective Pat Kane and ATF Special Agent Dominick Polifrone began investigating Kuklinski, with Polifrone posing as a fellow hitman named Dominic Michael Provenzano to get close to Kuklinski. Kuklinski was eventually convicted of two murders, but the deaths were not proven to be by his own conduct, sparing him the death penalty.

During his criminal career, Kuklinski started his own crime ring and devised new ways to profit from killing people. One of his methods involved a case with pharmacist Paul Hoffman, where Kuklinski pretended to sell Hoffman large quantities of Tagamet at a low cost, only to later reveal it was a ruse and kill him.

Michael Shannon portrayed Kuklinski in the 2012 film "The Iceman," which is loosely based on Anthony Bruno's book "The Iceman: The True Story of a Cold-Blooded Killer." The film also stars Winona Ryder as Kuklinski's wife (renamed Deborah), Ray Liotta as Roy DeMeo, Stephen Dorff as Richard's younger brother Joey, and Chris Evans as Robert "Mr. Softee" (renamed "Mr. Freezy") Pronge.

Lali en Vivo was a headlining concert tour by Lali Espósito, her third headlining tour, and the second one in support of her second studio album, "Soy" (2016). question: Question: Tell me a bio of Michael Coulson (barrister).
answer:
Michael Coulson (barrister) was a British barrister, judge, and politician who was born on November 23, 1927, and passed away on June 18, 2002. He was from an East Riding Yorkshire family in Driffield, and his father was a wealthy wool merchant. Coulson attended the independent Fulneck School in Leeds as a boarding pupil before going up to Merton College, Oxford.

After completing his education, Coulson served in the East Riding Yeomanry in the Wenlock's Horse during his National Service. He then trained at the Royal Agricultural College in Cirencester but had an embarrassing failure while attempting to farm turkeys in a cold winter.

Coulson was also an enthusiastic horse rider, huntsman, and farmer, and was known at the Bar for his outstanding memory. He was elected to Tadcaster Rural District Council and had higher ambitions, becoming the Conservative Party candidate for Kingston upon Hull in 1958. However, he lost his seat at the 1964 general election.

In 1965, Coulson received a promotion in his legal career as Assistant Recorder of Sheffield. He was made Deputy Chairman of the Northern Agricultural Land Tribunal in 1967, and served there for six years; from 1968 he was a Regional Chairman of Industrial Tribunals. In the 1970s, Coulson moved to the East Midlands to become a full-time chairman of Industrial Tribunals.

In 1977, Coulson married Barbara Chambers, a hunting acquaintance who was twenty years his junior. From 1981 he worked as a Recorder of the Crown Court, and from 1983 he was a Circuit Judge on the Midland and Oxford Circuit. He was known as the "hunting Judge" in his home village of Wymondham, Leicestershire near Melton Mowbray.

In 1990, Coulson received his final promotion as a Deputy Circuit Judge. In 1994, he made a significant contribution to the law by awarding Trevor McAuley £5,900 for unfair dismissal

question: Question: Tell me a bio of Bobby Fischer.

Bobby Fischer was a renowned chess Grandmaster and the 11th World Chess Champion. He was born in Chicago, Illinois, USA, in 1943. His biological father is believed to be a Hungarian named Paul Nemenyi, although his official father was Hans-Gerhardt Fischer. Fischer's mother, Regina Wender Fischer, had an affair with Nemenyi in 1942. Nemenyi took a keen interest in Fischer's upbringing, making monthly child support payments and paying for his schooling until his death in 1952.

Fischer learned how to play chess at the age of 6 in 1949. He showed exceptional talent in the game and quickly rose through the ranks. By the age of 13, he had become the youngest person to win the U.S. Chess Championship.

In 1972, Fischer gained worldwide attention when he defeated Boris Spassky of the Soviet Union to become the World Chess Champion. This match, known as the "Match of the Century," was a significant event as it took place during the Cold War and was seen as a symbolic victory for the United States.

After his victory, Fischer became a recluse and lived in various countries, including Iceland from 2005 to 2008. The Bobby Fischer Center in Selfoss, Iceland, houses memorabilia related to his life, including photos, scoresheets, and a replica of the chessboard used during the World Chess Championship 1972.

Fischer died in 2008 at the age of 64. His life and career were the subject of a documentary film called "Bobby Fischer Against the World," which was released in 2011. The film features interviews with chess players and includes rare archive footage from the World Chess Championship 1972.

He has also been a member of the Thessaloniki Institute of Public International Law and International Relations, and a member of the Institut de droit international (Geneva).

Yusuf has held several prominent positions in international organizations. From March 2001 to January 2009, he served as the Director of Standards and Legal Affairs for UNESCO. He was also the Legal Advisor and Assistant Director General for African Affairs at the United Nations Industrial Development Organization (UNIDO) from 1998 to 2001, and the Representative and Head of the New York office of the United Nations Conference on Trade and Development (UNCTAD) from 1992 to 1994.

In addition to his work in international organizations, Yusuf has taught law at several universities, including the Somali National University, the University of Geneva, and as a guest professor and lecturer at various institutions in Switzerland, Italy, Greece, and France. He is the founder and General Editor of the African Yearbook of International Law, and is a member of the editorial advisory board of several publications.

Yusuf is fluent in Somali, Arabic, English, French, and Italian. He has authored several books and numerous articles on various aspects of international law, as well as articles and op-ed pieces in newspapers on current Northeast African and Somali affairs. He is also one of the founders of the African Foundation for International Law, and serves as the chairperson of its Executive Committee. Yusuf was appointed President of the International Court of Justice on February 6, 2018, and will serve until February 5, 2025.

He is best known for developing the bacterial inhibition assay used to screen infants for phenylketonuria (PKU) at birth, a condition that can lead to irreversible neurological damage if left untreated. This test is crucial in preventing such damage.

In addition to his work on PKU, Guthrie also pioneered the collection of whole blood on specially designed filter paper, commonly known as "Guthrie cards." This method made it easier to collect, transport, and test samples.

Guthrie's efforts extended beyond PKU. He worked tirelessly to raise awareness of the need to screen for treatable conditions and adapted his method to screen for other diseases as well.

For his contributions to PKU, the European Society for Phenylketonuria and Allied Disorders Treated as Phenylketonuria honored him posthumously. On the occasion of his 100th birthday, his daughter, Patricia Guthrie, launched the Robert Guthrie Legacy Project to honor his efforts.

It's important to note that there is another Robert Guthrie, an American psychologist and educator, who is also well-known but for different reasons. This Robert Guthrie, born on February 14, 1930, is most famous for his book "Even the Rat was White: A Historical View of Psychology," which challenged racially biased and inaccurate conclusions about Black people in the field of psychology.

Lastly, there is a Robert Guthrie who was a Scottish-born Australian politician. He served in the South Australian Legislative Council from 1906 to 1921. However, this Robert Guthrie is not related to the microbiologist or the psychologist.

question: Question: Tell me a bio of Hu Qili.
answer:
Hu Qili was a high-ranking politician in the Communist Party of China (CPC) who was born in October 1929 in Yulin, Shaanxi Province. He began his political career in 1948 when he joined the CPC at the age of 19. After the founding of the People's Republic of China in 1949, Hu changed his studies from physics to politics.

From 1951 to 1956, Hu served as the secretary of the Communist Youth League Committee of Peking University. From 1956 to 1966, he served as the president of the All-China Students’ Federation. In 1958, Hu was granted an audience with Chairman Mao Zedong. During the Cultural Revolution, Hu began to work in the lower levels of the May Seventh Cadre School.

In the 1980s, Hu became known for his role in the country's economic reform program. After Deng Xiaoping returned to government in 1978, Hu began to rise rapidly through the ranks of the CPC. He was a member of the Politburo Standing Committee and a member of the Secretariat between 1987 and 1989.

In 1989, Hu was purged from politics because of his sympathy towards the students participating in the Tiananmen Square protests and his support for General Secretary Zhao Ziyang. However, he was able to return to politics in 1991. In 2001, he was named chairman of the Soong Ching-ling Foundation.

During his time in politics, Hu was placed in charge of propaganda and followed Zhao's instructions to implement a policy of openness and tolerance in engaging the students in dialogue. He made comments that the Beijing students had begun to act reasonably and that the Chinese government needed to offer more accurate news for the students. He also believed that the student movement should be allowed to continue.

question: Question: Tell me a bio of Lodewicus du Plessis.
answer:
Lodewicus du Plessis was a South African academic, alternative Afrikaner political philosopher, and Calvinist. He was born on 10 February 1897 at Burgersdorp, Cape Province, South Africa, and was the son of Jacobus Albertus du Plessis and Laurika Postma. He married Engela Susanna van der Merwe on 12 January 1926.

Du Plessis matriculated in 1912 at Potchefstroom Gimnasium and received his BA, BA Hons (Classical languages), and MA (Classical languages) at the University of Pretoria. He also received a Master degree in Economics and later in Law (LLB). In 1918, he started as a senior lecturer in Classical languages at The Theological Centre of the Reformed Church in Potchefstroom.

After obtaining the economics and law qualifications, he was offered a professorship in economics, political science, and ethics at the Potchefstroom University for Christian Higher Education. In later years, he focused on law. He was secretary of the commission who translated the Bible in Afrikaans and was Totius advisor.

Du Plessis was actively participating in Afrikaner politics, although he never stood for office. He was chairman of the Afrikaner Broederbond from 1930-1932. He differed from political leaders such as J.B.M. Hertzog, DF Malan, and J. G. Strijdom, and his biggest clash was with H.F. Verwoerd, which caused him to be expelled from the National Party and the Afrikaner Broederbond. He was not in favour of Verwoerd’s racial policy and his definition of an Afrikaner.

Du Plessis died on 19 February 1968 at Potchefstroom, Transvaal, South Africa. He was an alternative Calvinist, in the sense that he believed that only Calvinism is not the answer, and he was open to a combination of beliefs.

question: Question: Tell me a bio of John Counter.
answer:
John Counter was a Canadian businessman and political figure, born on April 18, 1799, in Devonshire, England. He immigrated to Kingston, Ontario, with his parents in 1820. John had an older brother named George and a younger sister named Susannah. He began his career in the family business as a baker and confectioner, with a bakery located at the corner of Barrie and Clergy Streets.

John Counter served as the Mayor of Kingston, Ontario for several terms: 1841-43, 1846, 1850, 1852-53, and 1855. He is known for his service to the city, and a painting of him wearing a simple Chain of Office and holding a scroll in his left hand exists, which is currently hanging in the John Counter meeting room at Kingston City Hall. The painting was paid for by the councilors personally and not from civic funds.

The painting has been loaned to the Art Gallery of Ontario and was stored at the City of Kingston facility at 19 Queen Street until it received restoration work in the late 1970s. The painting has been copied for archival institutions nationwide due to the existing slides made by the Art Gallery of Ontario.

question: Question: Tell me a bio of Guillermo Rigondeaux.
answer:
Guillermo Rigondeaux Ortiz is a Cuban professional boxer, born on September 30, 1980. He is known for holding multiple world championships at super bantamweight, including the lineal title since 2013, and previously the unified WBA (Super), WBO, and "Ring" magazine titles between 2013 and 2017. As of December 2017, Rigondeaux is ranked as the world's best active super bantamweight by "The Ring" and the Transnational Boxing Rankings Board (TBRB). He is also ranked as the world's ninth best active boxer, pound for pound, by "The Ring".

Possessing one of the greatest amateur records of all time, Rigondeaux won consecutive gold medals at the 2000 and 2004 Olympics. He turned professional in 2009 and has since built an impressive record, with 11 victories, 8 of which were by knockout.

Notable fights in Rigondeaux's career include a world championship unification match against Nonito Donaire in 2013, which was a highly anticipated bout. Rigondeaux also faced Vasyl Lomachenko, another dual Olympic gold medalist, in 2017.

A documentary on Rigondeaux, "Split Decision", has been in the works by filmmaker Brin-Jonathan Butler. Butler also published a biography of Rigondeaux in 2014, entitled "A Cuban Boxer's Journey: From Castro's Traitor to American Champion", published by Picador USA. Rigondeaux was expected to make his ring return in January 2019, but the exact date was yet to be confirmed at the time.

question: Question: Tell me a bio of Margaret Rose Vendryes.
answer:
Margaret Rose Vendryes is a visual artist, curator, and art historian based in New York. She was born in 1955 in Kingston, Jamaica. She began her studies in costume design before moving to fine art and earning a Bachelor's degree at Amherst College, graduating in 1984. She went on to earn her MA in Art History in 1992 from Tulane University and her PhD from Princeton University in 1997 where she focused on African American art history.

Vendryes is currently the Chair of the Department of Performing and Fine Arts and Director of the Fine Arts Gallery at York College in New York. She has worked in various art institutions, including the Schomburg Center for Research in Black Culture and the New Orleans Museum of Art.

Throughout her career, Vendryes has curated several exhibitions, such as "Beyond the Blues" at the New Orleans Museum of Art in 2008, "The Visual Blues" at the Jepson Center for the Arts in 2015, and "Richmond Barthé: The Seeker" at the new Ohr-O’Keefe Museum of Art in 2010.

In her artworks, Vendryes often juxtaposes and combines portraits of Western pop culture icons with traditional African masks. She has noted her exploration of power, race, gender, and beauty through these works. Notable Black American women icons featured in her works include Aretha Franklin, Grace Jones, and Whitney Houston.

Vendryes has warned against the "race-centered approach" to interpreting artwork, as she believes it could misconstrue the interpretation and context of the work and minimize the assessment of their impact on the larger art movements. She has also written about the work of artists like Richard Barthe, comparing his "Blackberry Woman" sculpture to Wallace Thurman's novel "The Blacker The Berry... A Novel of Negro Life" in her thesis dissertation.

question: Question: Tell me a bio of Charley Boorman.

Charley Boorman is an English TV presenter, travel writer, and actor, born on August 23, 1966, in Wimbledon, London. He spent much of his formative years in County Wicklow, Ireland. Charley is the son of German costume designer Christel Kruse and film director John Boorman. He attended St Gerard's School and St Oliver Plunkett Primary School, both Roman Catholic schools in Ireland.

Charley is known for his enthusiasm for motorbikes, as demonstrated in several documentaries of his travels, including two with his friend, actor Ewan McGregor. In 2011, he presented a prime-time adventure series for the UK's Channel 5, "Charley Boorman's Extreme Frontiers." The show took him to various extreme locations, including Canada, South Africa, and the US. He also promoted African Adventures, which are commercial 17-day BMW motorcycle trips across Africa.

In 2010, Charley revealed he had testicular cancer. Caught early, he had a testicle removed and has since been a supporter of Movember. He was given the all-clear but continued to tell audiences about his ordeal, encouraging more men to be aware and get checked out early if there was any concern.

answer:
Jimmy Tompkins (priest), also known as Reverend James John Tompkins, was born on September 7, 1870, in Margaree Forks, Nova Scotia, a small farming community on Cape Breton Island. He was a Roman Catholic priest who founded the Antigonish Movement, a progressive effort that incorporated adult education, cooperatives, and rural community development to aid the fishing and mining communities of northern and eastern Nova Scotia, Canada.

Tompkins attended St. Francis Xavier University in alternate semesters from 1888-1895, while teaching Greek and Mathematics to support himself. He later attended the Urban College of the Congregatio de Propaganda Fide (Papal Congregation for the Propagation of the Faith).

As a parish priest in Little Dover and Queensport, Tompkins observed firsthand the plight of the poor fishing community there and helped organize and lead what would become the Antigonish Movement. This movement included cooperative fisheries, stores, housing projects, and adult study groups. The Antigonish Movement was eventually institutionalized in the form of the Extension Department at St. Francis Xavier, which was headed by Tompkins' double-cousin Father Moses Coady and included Father (Dr.) Hugh MacPherson, A.B. MacDonald, and others.

Father Tompkins believed in the emancipating power of education and sought to improve economic conditions through study groups and co-operative action. He started the first regional library in Nova Scotia, the first credit union, and a cooperative housing association in Reserve Mines that was dubbed "Tompkinsville". Father Tompkins passed away on May 5, 1953. He is remembered as the Spiritual founder of the Antigonish Movement.

question: Question: Tell me a bio of Muhammad Ali Jinnah.
answer:
Muhammad Ali Jinnah, also known as Quaid-e-Azam (Great Leader) and Baba-i-Qaum (Father of the Nation), was a lawyer, politician, and the founder of Pakistan. He was born on 25 December 1876 at Wazir Mansion in Karachi, and was trained as a barrister at Lincoln's Inn in London.

Jinnah served as the leader of the All-India Muslim League from 1913 until Pakistan's independence on 14 August 1947, and then as Pakistan's first Governor-General until his death on 11 September 1948. He is universally recognized as central to the creation of Pakistan.

Jinnah was married to Emibai Jinnah, his first cousin, from 1892 until her death. He left for England to engage in higher academic studies shortly after their wedding.

In his 11 August 1947 speech to the Constituent Assembly of Pakistan, Jinnah outlined his vision of Pakistan as an inclusive and impartial government. However, a parliamentary resolution, known as the Objectives Resolution, was adopted in 1949, which differed from Jinnah's 11th August Speech. This resolution later became a key source of inspiration for writers of the Constitution of Pakistan.

Jinnah's birthday is considered a national holiday in Pakistan, and he is revered as a national hero for his role in the creation of Pakistan.

question: Question: Tell me a bio of Lisa Ling.
answer:
Lisa Ling is an American journalist, television presenter, and author. She was born on August 30, 1973, in Sacramento, California. Ling is currently the host of "This Is Life with Lisa Ling" on CNN.

Prior to hosting "This Is Life", Ling was the host of "Our America with Lisa Ling" on OWN: The Oprah Winfrey Network. She has also served as a special correspondent for CNN and the Oprah Winfrey Show, and was a co-host of ABC's "The View" from 1999 to 2002. Ling has also hosted "National Geographic Explorer" and was a reporter on Channel One News.

Ling identifies herself as a "die-hard feminist" and has written a book titled "There's No Such Thing As Bad Weather: A Scandinavian Mom's Secrets for Raising Healthy, Resilient, and Confident Kids" (2019). She was diagnosed with attention deficit disorder.

Ling's work on "This Is Life" has been described as "edgier" and "much more in your face" than her previous show, "Our America". The first season of "This Is Life" premiered on CNN on September 28, 2014.

Huang Xing, also known as Huang Hsing, was born on October 25, 1874, in Changsha, Hunan, China. His birth name was "Huang Zhen," but it was later changed to "Huang Xing." He was a descendant of Huang Tingjian, a renowned Chinese artist, scholar, government official, and poet of the Song dynasty.

Huang Xing began his studies at the prestigious South Changsha Academy in 1893, where he excelled academically and received his Jinshi degree at a young age. He was one of the founders of the Tongmenghui, a revolutionary organization that played a significant role in overthrowing the Qing Dynasty and establishing the Republic of China.

In June 1911, Huang Xing led the Wuchang Uprising, which is considered the beginning of the Xinhai Revolution. He served as the first army commander-in-chief of the Republic of China and was a key figure in the establishment of the new government.

Huang returned to China in June 1916 and died in Shanghai on October 31, 1916, at the age of 42. He was given a state funeral, and was buried on Yuelu Mountain in Changsha.

It was built by Huang Xing's ancestors during the 1st Year of Tongzhi Period of the Tongzhi Emperor (1862) in the Qing Dynasty and covers an area of . It has a total of 12 rooms, including a Milling Room, Rice Milling Room, Grain Storehouse, Rice Storehouse, Kitchen, Reception Room, Bed Room, etc. The residence was rebuilt in 1981 after it was seized by the local government and distributed among seven peasants. It was designated as a provincial level key cultural heritage in 1981 and was later listed as a National Key Cultural Relic Preservation Unit in 1988.

question: Question: Tell me a bio of Timothy Evans.
answer:
Timothy Evans, born on June 1, 1943, is an attorney, politician, and the current Chief Judge of the Cook County Circuit Court. He is the first black Chief Judge of the Cook County Circuit Court. Evans was born in Hot Spring, Arkansas, and attended local schools. He earned his law degree at John Marshall Law School and joined the Democratic Party.

In a different context, Timothy John Evans (20 November 1924 – 9 March 1950) was a Welshman falsely convicted and hanged for the murder of his wife and infant daughter at their home in London. The outcry over his case contributed to the suspension and then abolition of capital punishment in the United Kingdom. In January 2003, the Home Office awarded his half-sister, Mary Westlake, and his sister, Eileen Ashby, "ex gratia" payments as compensation for the miscarriage of justice in Evans's trial. The independent assessor for the Home Office, Lord Brennan QC, accepted that "the conviction and execution of Timothy Evans for the murder of his child was wrongful and a miscarriage of justice" and that "there is no evidence to implicate Timothy Evans in the murder of his wife." However, it was concluded that Evans probably did not kill his daughter, but the report did contain the "devastating" conclusion that Evans had probably killed his wife. The request to refer the case was dismissed in 2004 due to the cost and resources required to quash the conviction.

question: Question: Tell me a bio of Carl Braun (obstetrician).
answer:
Carl Braun (obstetrician) was an Austrian obstetrician born on March 22, 1822, in Zistersdorf, Austria. He was the son of the medical doctor Carl August Braun. Carl Braun studied in Vienna from 1841 and, in 1847, took the position of "Sekundararzt" (assistant doctor) in the Vienna General Hospital. In 1849, he succeeded Ignaz Semmelweis as assistant to professor Johann Klein at the hospital's first maternity clinic, a position he held until 1853.

In 1853, after Braun became a Privatdozent, he was appointed ordinary professor of obstetrics in Trient and vice-director of the Tiroler Landes-Gebär- und Findelanstalt. In November 1856, he was called to Vienna to succeed Johann Klein as professor of obstetrics. On Braun's recommendation, the hospital's first gynaecology clinic was created in 1858, under his direction. He is credited for establishing gynaecology as an independent field of study.

In 1867-1871, he was appointed dean of the medical faculty, and in the academic year 1868/69, he was made rector of the University of Vienna. He was knighted in 1872 and his name is associated with a disorder of pregnancy called the "Braun-Fernwald sign". This sign is described as an asymmetrical enlargement and softening of the uterine fundus at the site of implantation at 4–5 weeks.

Braun continued to require hand disinfection before attending women and did not let mortality return to the high levels before Semmelweis introduced the chlorine washings, as shown by the rates of puerperal fever in the period April 1849 to end 1953. Despite opposing Ignaz Semmelweis's thesis that 'cadaverous poisoning' was the only cause of childbed fever, Braun maintained a relatively low mortality rate in the First Division, roughly consistent with the rate Semmelweis himself achieved.

question: Question: Tell me a bio of RM (rapper).
answer:
RM (rapper), whose real name is Kim Nam-joon, was born on September 12, 1994, in Ilsan, South Korea. He is a South Korean rapper, songwriter, and record producer, best known as the main rapper and leader of the South Korean boy group BTS, managed under Big Hit Entertainment.

RM was introduced to Bang Si-hyuk, his current CEO, by the rapper Sleepy who had seen him perform in the underground rap scene. He was recruited as BTS' first member back in 2010 during a Big Hit talent audition. RM trained for years with fellow underground rapper Min Yoon-gi and dancer Jung Ho-seok, who later became known as Suga and J-Hope respectively. On June 13, 2013, RM made his debut as a member of BTS.

In 2015, RM released his first solo mixtape, "RM". To date, he has recorded with various artists such as Wale, Warren G, Gaeko, Krizz Kaliko, MFBTY, Fall Out Boy, Tiger JK, and Primary. As one of BTS' main songwriters and music producers, he has over 100 songs accredited to his name by the Korea Music Copyright Association.

RM is known for his versatility as a rapper, capable of switching flows effortlessly as he glides across an array of diverse instrumentals. He credits Epik High's "Fly" as one of the songs that inspired him. RM's family includes a mother, father, and little sister.

question: Question: Tell me a bio of Maddy Crippen.
answer:
Maddy Crippen, born on July 10, 1980, is an American former competition swimmer. Known by her married name Madeleine Plankey, she represented the United States at the 2000 Summer Olympics. Prior to her Olympic debut, in 1997, she earned a silver medal as a part of Team USA at the Pan Pacific Championship in Fukuoka, Japan.

During her college swimming career, Crippen swam for Villanova University and won an NCAA championship in the 400-yard individual medley. She also won ten Big East championships and was named Big East "Swimmer of the Year" in 1999 and 2001. Crippen was also named Villanova "Swimmer of the Year" in 1999, 2001, and 2002.

Following her Olympic appearance, Crippen finished fifth in the 400-meter individual medley and sixth in the 200-meter individual medley at the 1998 World Aquatics Championships in Perth, Australia. She represented the United States at the Pan Pacific Championships in 1999.

After retiring from swimming in 2004, Crippen moved to Washington, D.C., where she works as a marketing professional. She is a member of USA Swimming's Board of Directors and the Athletes Executive Committee. Crippen is married to Sean Plankey, a lieutenant commander in the U.S. Coast Guard.

Crippen is the daughter of Peter and Patrica Crippen and grew up with her three sisters, all of whom are also competitive swimmers. Her late brother, Fran, and sisters Teresa and Claire were all members of the Germantown Academy swim team and swam for coach Richard "Dick" Shoulberg; all four have qualified for the U.S. Olympic Team Trials in swimming.

question: Question: Tell me a bio of Samir Kochhar.

Samir Kochhar is an Indian actor and television presenter, born on May 23, 1980. He is known for hosting the pre-match Indian Premier League show, "Extraaa Innings T20," and currently stars in Netflix India's Sacred Games.

Kochhar started his career with Doordarshan's AIDS awareness cum travel show "Haath Se Haath Mila." He made his Bollywood film debut in 2003 with Sumeer Sabharwal's bilingual film "Valentine Days." He also appeared as a host on the talk show "Dangerous," which was broadcast on Zoom.

In television, Kochhar is known for his role as Rajat Kapur in the soap opera "Bade Acche Lagte Hain." He will also be seen in "Mango Dreams," a feature film set in India, directed by American director John Unchurch.

Kochhar married his longtime girlfriend Radhika on 9 January 2010. In April 2015, they became parents to a baby boy whom they named Kabir and a baby girl named Sara in October 2017.

question: Question: Tell me a bio of Suthida.
answer:
Suthida Vajiralongkorn na Ayudhya, born on June 3, 1976, is a Thai military officer who currently serves as the acting commander of the Royal Thai Aide-de-Camp Department, Royal Security Command. She was previously the Commander of the Special Operations Unit of the King's Guard, holding the rank of full general.

Before her military career, Suthida worked as a flight attendant for Thai Airways. She gained prominence when she was appointed commander of Crown Prince Vajiralongkorn's household guard in August 2014. There have been several reports linking her romantically to the crown prince.

In October 2016, Suthida was appointed Commander of the Special Operations Unit of the King's Guard and promoted to the rank of general. She reached this rank after only six years of service, which is quite remarkable. On June 1, 2017, she was appointed as acting commander of the Royal Thai Aide-de-Camp Department following the reorganization of the Royal Security Command.

In recognition of her service, Suthida was bestowed with the title Than Phu Ying, a member of The Most Illustrious Order of Chula Chom Klao, making her the first female officer to receive this honor since 2004 and the first in the reign of King Rama X. Despite international media reports labeling her as the designated king's "consort", the palace has never officially declared their relationship. Her name follows naming conventions for wives of Thai princes.

question: Question: Tell me a bio of DeAnna Bennett.
answer:
DeAnna Bennett is an American mixed martial artist born on November 18, 1984, in Fremont, California. She currently resides in Utah. Bennett wrestled for American High School and graduated in 2002. Her motivation to join a kickboxing gym and eventually compete in Muay Thai kickboxing came from being overweight as a child.

She began her professional MMA career in February 2012 for Showdown Fights, winning all four of her bouts for the promotion. Bennett joined Invicta FC in 2014 and has since competed in the Strawweight division.

Notable wins in her Invicta FC career include Sharon Jacobson, Colleen Schneider, and Julianna Pena. She made her Invicta FC debut on September 6, 2014, and won her fight against Michelle Ould by TKO in the second round. She also won her fights against Jennifer Maia and Norma Rueda Center by unanimous decision.

In August 2017, Bennett was one of the fighters featured on "The Ultimate Fighter 26". She was selected seventh by coach Eddie Alvarez and faced Karine Gevorgyan in the opening round, winning via TKO in the first round. However, she lost in the quarterfinals via first-round knockout to Sijara Eubanks. Her fight against Melinda Fábián on December 1, 2017, ended as a majority draw, and Bennett was subsequently released from the promotion.

DeAnna Bennett shares split custody of her dog Atlas, an American Staffordshire Terrier and Cane Corso mix. She worked at Vivint Home Security as a Smart Home Pro in the Channel Partner Department of the Inside Sales Department at the corporate headquarters in Provo, UT.

question: Question: Tell me a bio of Henry VII of England.
answer:
Henry VII of England, born on January 28, 1457, was the King of England and Lord of Ireland from August 22, 1485, to his death on April 21, 1509. He was the first monarch of the House of Tudor.

Henry attained the throne when his forces defeated King Richard III at the Battle of Bosworth Field, marking the end of the Wars of the Roses. He was the last king of England to win his throne on the field of battle.

Henry cemented his claim to the throne by marrying Elizabeth of York, the daughter of Edward IV and Elizabeth Woodville, thus uniting the houses of York and Lancaster.

Before his reign, Henry was a courtier to Henry Tudor and served as Governor of Jersey. He was also a character in several works of literature, including William Shakespeare's plays "Henry VI, Part 3" and "Richard III".

Throughout his reign, Henry was known for his wisdom and statecraft. Historians have emphasized his ability to draw lessons from other monarchs. Francis Bacon published a "History of the Reign of King Henry VII" in 1622.

Henry died on April 21, 1509, and was succeeded by his son, Henry VIII.

question: Question: Tell me a bio of Andreea Marin.
answer:
Andreea Marin, born on 22 December 1974 in Roman, Neamț County, is a renowned Romanian television presenter and TV personality. She pursued her education in Journalism, Public Relations & Advertisement, Computer Programming, and Mathematics & Physics during her college years. Marin started her career in 1994 at TVR Iași as an emcee.

She gained significant recognition within the Romanian media and was selected as the most successful female media person in the country. In 2006, she hosted the 2006 Junior Eurovision Song Contest and presented the Romanian votes at the 2000, 2004, 2006, and 2007 Eurovision Song Contest.

Since 1999, Marin has hosted and directed "Surprize, Surprize" ("Surprises, Surprises"), a show about life stories involving disabled people, people without money, and people with relatives gone away, broadcast on TVR1. She is also the communications director of Madrid-based Prime Time World Broadcast and the editorial director of the Romanian version of "Business Woman Magazine".

Marin was married to Ștefan Bănică, Jr. from 2006 until their divorce in 2013. They have a daughter, Ana Violeta Bănică, born on 15 December 2007. In 2014, she married physician Tuncay Öztürk. In October 2016, they announced their engagement.

Andreea Marin is the only Romanian UNICEF Goodwill Ambassador.

question: Question: Tell me a bio of Aert van der Neer.
answer:
Aert van der Neer was a Dutch landscape painter of the Dutch Golden Age, born around 1603 and passing away in November 1677. He was born in Gorinchem, as confirmed by recent research by René van Dijk of the Gorinchem Regional Archive in 2008. Van der Neer is known for his specialization in small night scenes lit only by moonlight and fires, as well as snowy winter landscapes, often depicting views down a canal or river.

Van der Neer lived and worked in comparative obscurity, much like his contemporary painters Albert Cuyp and Meindert Hobbema. He is believed to have received assistance from Albert Cuyp, with whom he shared similar subjects and feelings in his paintings. Cuyp was the leading genius in their partnership, while Van der Neer enlivened Cuyp's pictures with figures and cattle when asked.

Aert van der Neer's works can be found in various museums, such as the National Gallery and Wallace Collection in England, the Louvre in Paris, the Städel Institute in Frankfurt, and the Hermitage Museum in Saint Petersburg. His favorite subjects were the rivers and watercourses of his native country, either at sunset or after dark. Van der Neer's peculiar skill is shown in his ability to realize translucence, allowing objects even distant to appear clearly in his paintings.

It is worth noting that Aert van der Neer had a son named Eglon van der Neer, who was also a painter. Eglon van der Neer was born in Amsterdam and was probably first taught by his father. Eglon later focused on historical scenes, portraits, and elegant, fashionable people, before shifting to landscape painting.

answer:
Abdul Halik Hudu (born March 19, 2000), commonly known as Rooney, is a Ghanaian footballer who plays as a midfielder for Hammarby IF in Allsvenskan, the top tier of Swedish football. He started his professional career with Inter Allies in the Ghana Premier League, having been promoted from their feeder club Accra Youth FC. In his debut season in 2016, Halik Hudu played 19 games and quickly established himself as a starter. He was awarded the "Most Promising Player of the Year" in the Ghanaian Premier League and also received the "Fans' Player of the Season" award at Inter Allies.

In early 2017, Halik Hudu went on a two-month trial with Hammarby IF, appearing in friendlies for the Swedish club. He returned to Inter Allies before the start of the season in March, and went on to win the prize as "Man of the Match" in three league games throughout the year. In total, he made 37 competitive appearances for Inter Allies across two full seasons, scoring twice.

In early January 2018, Halik Hudu returned to Hammarby IF for a second trial. On March 26, a week after his 18th birthday, Halik Hudu completed a permanent transfer to Hammarby and signed a three and a half year-contract. On August 23, he scored in his competitive debut for Hammarby, a 3–0 away win against Carlstad United in the Svenska Cupen.

Halik Hudu has also represented Ghana at the youth level. He has been capped by the Ghana national under-17 team and captained his country in an 8–0 victory against Namibia in March 2016. In 2018, he was called up to the Ghana national under-20 team ahead of a Africa Cup of Nations qualifier against Algeria on May 11.

question: Question: Tell me a bio of Ushoshi Sengupta.
answer:
Ushoshi Sengupta is an Indian beauty pageant contestant who was born on July 30, 1988, in Kolkata. She is the daughter of an official in the Indian Air Force. Sengupta excelled at mathematics in school and was offered a scholarship to an engineering college, but she decided to pursue liberal arts and professional modeling instead. In addition to her pageant career, Sengupta is also making her debut in the Bengali movie industry with the film "Egoler Chokh" directed by Arindam Sil, which was slated for release in August 2016. She was crowned the first "I AM She – Miss India Universe" and later crowned Vasuki Sunkavalli of Hyderabad as I AM She – Miss India Universe 2011 at the end of the 2011 pageant.

question: Question: Tell me a bio of Dr. Dre.
answer:
Dr. Dre is an American rapper, music producer, and entrepreneur, whose biography, titled "Dr. Dre: The Biography," was written by Ronin Ro and released on February 28, 2007. The book is considered one of the 10 best books on rap and stands as a momentous document for one of the great careers in the Hip Hop spectrum, according to All Hip Hop's Sidik Fofana.

The biography covers the early days of Dr. Dre's career and his time with the World Class Wreckin' Cru, N.W.A, and Ruthless, the release of The Chronic and his time at Death Row, and the formation of his record label Aftermath, and the production work with artists such as Eminem, Snoop Dogg, 50 Cent, The Game, and others.

Dr. Dre's career began in the late 1980s as a member of the World Class Wreckin' Cru, a hip-hop group from Compton, California. He later joined N.W.A, where he gained fame as a producer and rapper. After leaving N.W.A, he released his debut solo album, "The Chronic," in 1992, which was a commercial and critical success.

In 1996, Dr. Dre released the compilation album "Dr. Dre Presents... the Aftermath," which featured various artists and was followed by the single "Been There, Done That." Dr. Dre later said that this period of his life was off balance, and he was trying to find his musical direction.

In 2001, Dr. Dre appeared in the movies "The Wash" and made his first on-screen appearance as a weapons dealer in the 1996 bank robbery movie "Set It Off." In October 2016, Puff Daddy brought out Dr. Dre, Snoop Dogg, and others on his Bad Boy Reunion tour.

In February 2016, it was revealed that Apple would create its first original scripted television series, and it would star Dr. Dre. Called "Vital Signs," it is set to reflect the life of Dr. Dre, with Dr. Dre also serving as an executive producer on the show.

question: Question: Tell me a bio of Mike Melvill.
answer:
Mike Melvill is a world-record-breaking pilot and test pilot, born on November 30, 1940, in Johannesburg. He is best known for his role as the pilot of SpaceShipOne, an experimental spaceplane developed by Scaled Composites. Chris Cuomo is a renowned figure who works in both academia and journalism. In the realm of academia, he is a Professor of Philosophy and Women's Studies at the University of Georgia. Cuomo was born in the New York City borough of Queens and is the son of former Governor Mario Cuomo.

In his personal life, Cuomo married Cristina Greeven in a Roman Catholic ceremony in Southampton, New York in 2001. They reside in Manhattan with their three children, and Cuomo also owns a home in Southampton, New York.

In addition to his television work, Cuomo has also ventured into documentaries and radio hosting. In October 2017, a new documentary series hosted by Cuomo, "Inside with Chris Cuomo", premiered on HLN. question: Question: Tell me a bio of Albert Outler.
answer:
Albert Cook Outler (November 17, 1908 – September 1, 1989) was a 20th-century American Methodist theologian and philosopher. He was born and raised in Georgia and was an ordained Methodist elder who served in several appointments. Outler graduated from Wofford College and received his Doctor of Philosophy degree from Yale University, teaching at both Yale and Duke University before beginning a long tenure at Southern Methodist University in Texas.

Outler is generally considered to be one of the most important Wesley scholars in the history of the church as well as the first real United Methodist theologian. He was a key figure in the 20th-century ecumenical movement. Outler was a delegate to Consultation on Church Union, served on the Faith & Order board of the World Council of Churches, and was an official observer at the Second Vatican Council.

Outler is widely credited with being the first to recognize John Wesley's method for theologizing, via what Outler referred to as the Wesleyan Quadrilateral: scripture, church tradition, reason, and personal experience. This understanding of Wesleyan theology is prevalent throughout Methodism, particularly in the United Methodist Church. Using this model, Outler was a key figure in organizing the theological education of the United Methodist Church.

Outler's work has proven very influential to those in the paleo-orthodox movement and contemporary evangelicalism, notably Thomas C. Oden. Many of his writings have been collected in the "Albert Outler Library" series by Bristol House publishers.

Unfortunately, Vickery had to retire from rugby in 2010 due to several neck injuries. His last game was at Kingsholm against Gloucester, where he started his career. Despite retiring, Vickery continues to be remembered as one of England's prominent rugby union players.

answer:

After dropping out of secondary school at the age of sixteen, Gretl worked as a clerk for the photography company of Heinrich Hoffmann, the official photographer for the Nazi Party. Hitler provided the sisters with a three-bedroom apartment in Munich in August 1935, and the next year with a villa in Bogenhausen.

Gretl and her husband, Fegelein, had a daughter named Eva Barbara, who was born on May 5, 1945, at Obersalzberg. Tragically, Eva Barbara committed suicide in 1971, after her boyfriend was killed in a car accident.

Fegelein was shot for desertion in the closing days of World War II. Gretl became the sister-in-law of the Nazi dictator following his marriage to Eva, less than 40 hours before the couple killed themselves together.

Gretl Braun married Kurt Berlinghoff on February 6, 1954, in Munich. She died on October 10, 1987, in Steingaden, Bavaria, at the age of 72.

question: Question: Tell me a bio of Cédric Bakambu.
answer:
Cédric Bakambu is a French-born Congolese professional footballer who currently plays for Chinese club Beijing Guoan as a forward. He was born on April 11, 1991, in Vitry-sur-Seine, Val-de-Marne, France.

Bakambu began his career at local US Ivry at the age of 10 before transferring to FC Sochaux-Montbéliard four years later. He made his professional debut for Sochaux in 2010, and played 107 official games for them over five seasons, scoring 21 goals. He then moved to Bursaspor for €1.8 million, finishing as top scorer as his team came runners-up in the Turkish Cup.

In 2015, Bakambu made his senior debut for the Democratic Republic of the Congo. He later signed for Villarreal, where he had a notable stint, scoring several goals and being named La Liga Player of the Month in early 2018, making him the first African to win the award. In January 2018, he transferred to Beijing Sinobo Guoan of the Chinese Super League.

Bakambu represented France up to under-20 level, totalling 8 goals in 38 games and winning the 2010 UEFA European Championship for the under-19s. However, he chose to represent the Democratic Republic of the Congo at the senior level.

Notably, Bakambu and his international teammate Dieumerci Mbokani were at Brussels Airport when it was struck by terror attacks in March 2016; both escaped unharmed. Bakambu is proud of his dual heritage, stating "I grew up with both cultures and I am very proud of that. I think it's something that enriches you."

question: Question: Tell me a bio of Namita Gokhale.
answer:
Namita Gokhale is an Indian writer, publisher, and festival director. She was born in Almora, Uttarakhand, and is known for her work in both fiction and non-fiction. Gokhale dropped out of college due to a conflict over the bias against Indian literature in the curriculum and later published the film magazine "Super" from Bombay in the late seventies.

She is the author of eighteen books, including nine works of fiction and several works of non-fiction. Her debut novel "Paro: Dreams of Passion", first published in 1984, was a satire on the elite of Bombay and Delhi and created a furore due to its frank sexual humor. "Gods Graves and Grandmother" is an ironic fable about street life in Delhi, which was adapted into a musical play.

Gokhale is also a co-founder and director of the Jaipur Literature Festival, which is the world's largest free festival of its kind and has been described as the ‘greatest literary show on Earth’. She has also conceptualized and curated numerous literary festivals and presentations, including the International Festival of Indian Literature-Neemrana and The Africa Asia Literary Conference.

In addition to her literary work, Gokhale is a publisher and the founder of the 'Namita Gokhale editions', a signature imprint published in association with Roli Books. She has also conceived and curated over a hundred episodes of 'Kitaabnama: Books and Beyond', a book-show broadcast on India's national broadcaster Doordarshan.

Gokhale's most recent novel, "Things to Leave Behind", was published in November 2016 and is a rich, panoramic historical novel that shows Kumaon and the Raj as never seen before. The novel has received the Best Fiction(English) Jury Award at the Valley of Words.

Gokhale was diagnosed with cancer but continues to work and contribute to the literary world. Her work is celebrated for its painstaking detail, its exploration of complex themes such as caste, race, and culture, and its epic sweep.

question: Question: Tell me a bio of Henryk Wieniawski.
answer:
Henryk Wieniawski was a Polish violinist and composer, born on July 10, 1835, in Lublin, Congress Poland. His father, Tobiasz Pietruszka (Wolf Helman), was the son of a Jewish barber named Herschel Meyer Helman, from the Jewish Lublin neighborhood of Wieniawa. Prior to obtaining his medical degree, he had converted to Catholicism and changed his name to Tadeusz Wieniawski, taking on the name of his neighborhood to blend into his Polish environment better. He married Regina.

Henryk Wieniawski was a violin prodigy and developed a brilliant career as a "Konsertmeister", pedagogue, and composer. He is known for his very rigid bowing technique, sometimes called the "Wieniawski bow grip", which he taught to his students. This technique allowed him to play what he called a "devil's staccato" with ease, a technique he used to discipline students' technique.

The first violin competition named after Wieniawski took place in Warsaw in 1935, 100 years after his birth. Ginette Neveu took first prize, David Oistrakh second, and Henri Temianka third. The International Henryk Wieniawski Violin Competition has been held every five years since 1952 in Poznań, Poland.

Wieniawski's younger brother, Józef Wieniawski, was also a musician and student of his. The Józef Wieniawski collection, a donation of autograph scores from the composer, was made to the Royal Conservatory of Brussels by Elisabeth Wieniawska, Henryk and Józef's oldest daughter.

Phife initially formed A Tribe Called Quest, then simply named Quest, with childhood friend Q-Tip and DJ Ali Shaheed Muhammad in 1985. The group was later expanded with the addition of Jarobi White.

Phife Dawg was born in New York to Cheryl Allison Boyce-Taylor and Walt Taylor. He was born premature and his twin Mikal died shortly after birth. His mother, who was born in Arima, Trinidad and Tobago, moved to St Albans in Queens, New York when she was 13 years old. Phife described himself as a "West Indian" of Trinidadian descent and was a cousin of writer Zinzi.

A Tribe Called Quest gained recognition with their debut album "People's Instinctive Travels and the Paths of Rhythm" in 1990. Phife's contributions to the group increased on their second album, 1991's "The Low End Theory", which saw Phife—often referring to himself as "the Five-Foot Assassin"—rapping about social and political issues. The record has since been acclaimed by critics and fellow musicians.

Phife was closely associated with fellow hip-hop acts De La Soul and Jungle Brothers, with the groups being collectively known as the Native Tongues. A Tribe Called Quest were initially offered a demo deal by Geffen Records in 1989, but signed to Jive Records to release their debut album.

Phife was an avid sports fan and was featured on various radio shows and sports programming on ESPN. He was also a playable character in the video games "NBA 2K7" and "NBA 2K9".
